Functional Description

HBM3 DRAM Organization
                The HBM3 DRAM is optimized for high-bandwidth operation to a stack of multiple DRAM devices
                across a number of independent interfaces called channels. It is anticipated that each DRAM stack
                will support up to 16 channels.

Channel Definition
                A channel provides access to an independent set of DRAM banks. Requests from one channel do
                not access data in a different channel. Channels are individually clocked and need not to operate
                synchronously. Each channel consists of an independent command and data interface comprising




                                                                    A
                120 I/O signals. Reset and temperature signals are common to all channels. Refer to Table 1 for a
                list of per-channel signals and to Table 2 for global signals and those associated with the




                                                                   D
                IEEE1500 test access port.



                                                            rN
                The figure below shows an example stack containing four DRAM dies and one interface die. Each
                DRAM die comprises four channels and contributes additional capacity and additional channels to
                                                      de
                the stack, with a total of 16 channels per stack. The division of channels among the DRAM dies
                within a stack is irrelevant to the memory controller, and the example below is not a required
                                                un

                organization. The actual mapping of channels to memory dies is summarized in Table 4.

                Figure 4: HBM3 DRAM Stack With Channels

                Because each channel is independent, much of this document will describe a single channel.
                Where signal names are used, families of signals belonging to a given channel will have the suffix
                a, b, … , p for channels a through p; if no suffix is present, the signal(s) being described are
                generic instances of the various per-channel signals.

Pseudo Channel
                Each channel is further divided into two pseudo channels (PC). Both pseudo channels operate
                                         ed



                semi-independently: they share the channel’s row and column command bus as well as the CK
                clock but decode and execute commands individually as illustrated in the figure below: address bit
                                   id




                PC directs commands either to pseudo channel 0 (PC0) or pseudo channel 1 (PC1). Power-down
                and self refresh are common to both pseudo channels. Both pseudo channels also share the
                                 ov




                channel’s mode registers.
                Each pseudo channel provides 272-bit prefetch (256 data and 16 meta data bits) per memory read
                               Pr




                and write access. All I/O signals of DWORD0 are associated with PC0, and all I/O signals of
                DWORD1 are associated with PC1.

                                                                                                  Mode Registers

Mode Registers
                The mode registers define the specific mode of operation for the HBM3 DRAM. Sixteen 8-bit wide
                mode registers (MR0 to MR15) are defined. MR10 and MR12 are special mode registers and
                reserved for vendor specific features. Mode registers are common to both pseudo channels (PC0
                and PC1). Reprogramming the mode registers does not alter the contents of the memory array.
                Mode registers are programmed via the MODE REGISTER SET (MRS) command and retain the
                stored information until they are reprogrammed, chip reset, or until the device loses power. Mode
                Register can also be programmed via the IEEE1500 instruction MODE_REGISTER_DUMP_SET;
                this instruction can also be used to retrieve the Mode Register content.
                Mode registers must be loaded when all banks are idle and the time tRDMRS from a preceding
                READ command has elapsed. The controller must wait the specified time tMOD before initiating




                                                                    A
                any subsequent operations. Violating either of these requirements will result in unspecified




                                                                   D
                operation.



                                                            rN
                No default states are defined for mode registers except when otherwise noted. Users therefore
                must fully initialize all mode registers to the desired values upon power-up or after a subsequent
                chip reset.
                                                      de
                When an entire mode register is marked as RFU (“reserved for future use”), then it is considered as
                not supported by the HBM3 DRAM, and its content is Don’t Care.
                                                un

                Reserved states should not be used, as unknown operation or incompatibility with future versions
                may result. RFU bits in these registers must be programmed to 0.
                                         ed
                                   id
                                 ov
                               Pr

                                                                                                    Initialization

Initialization
                To power-up and initialize the HBM3 device into functional operation the sequence in the HBM3
                Power-Up and Initialization Sequence section must be followed.
                At any time after the power-up initialization, the HBM3 device may be reset using the sequence in
                the Initialization Sequence with Stable Power section. All IEEE 1500 port instructions may be used
                within the initialization sequences, as described in the Initialization Sequence For Use Of IEEE
                1500 Instructions Including Lane Repairs section.
                The interactions between HBM functional reset and the IEEE 1500 port reset are as follows:
                •    Functional reset requires that the IEEE 1500 port also be reset.
                •    The IEEE 1500 port can be reset at any time without impacting normal operation.




                                                                     A
                •    The IEEE 1500 port may be brought out of reset and a limited set of instructions may be used




                                                                    D
                     after a minimum time tINIT3 after RESET_n has been deasserted. See section Initialization



                                                             rN
                     Sequence For Use Of IEEE 1500 Instructions Including Lane Repairs
                •    If not needed, the IEEE 1500 port may be left in reset (WRST_n = LOW) during normal
                                                       de
                     operation.

HBM3 Power-Up and Initialization Sequence
                                                 un

                The HBM3 DRAM must be powered up and initialized in a predefined manner following the
                sequence below. Refer also to Figure 6.
                                          ed



                1. Apply power to the VDDC, VDDQ, VDDQL and VPP supplies following the requirements in the Power
                   Ramp Conditions table. VPP must ramp at the same time or earlier than VDDC and VDDQ. VDDC
                                   id




                   and VDDQ must ramp simultaneously and at the same time or earlier than VDDQL. During power
                                 ov




                   supply ramp time tINIT0, RESET_n, WRST_n and all other input signals may be in an
                   undefined state (driven LOW or HIGH, or High-Z). After Ta is reached, VDDC and VDDQ must be
                               Pr




                   greater than VDDQL -200mV. VDDC and VDDQ must be powered within 1 minute after power is
                   applied to VPP, and the total time for which VPP is powered and VDDC and VDDQ are unpowered
                   should not exceed 24 cumulative hours.
                2. RESET_n and WRST_n must be driven LOW (below 0.2 × VDDQ) before or at the same time
                   when tINIT0 expires. All other input signals may be in an undefined state (driven LOW or HIGH,
                   or High-Z) at this point. RESET_n must be maintained LOW for a minimum of tINIT1 time with
                   stable power. However, RESET_n must go HIGH within 1 minute after VDDC and VDDQ have
                   ramped and reached stable levels. After tINIT6 time has elapsed, the HBM3 device drives
                   RDQS_t and RDQS_c to LOW and HIGH static levels, respectively, and AERR, DERR and
                   CATTRIP signals LOW.
                3. A time tINIT2 before RESET_n is pulled HIGH, CK_t and CK_c must be driven to static LOW
                   and HIGH levels, respectively.
                4. After RESET_n is driven HIGH, R[3:0] must be driven to PDE state (HIGH, LOW, HIGH, LOW)
                   and C[2:0] must be driven to CNOP state (HIGH, HIGH, HIGH) a time tINIT7 before the CK
                   clock is started. R[9:4] and C[7:3] are allowed to remain in an undefined state. The HBM3
                   device resets into the precharged power-down state. During tINIT3, the HBM3 device will read
                   and apply internal fuse configuration data and perform I/O driver impedance calibration. At the
                   same time the WRST_n signal may be optionally driven HIGH to enable a subset of the IEEE
                   1500 instructions (see Initialization Sequence For Use Of IEEE1500 Instructions Including Lane
                   Repairs and Channel Disable and IEEE Standard 1500 sections). In that case, all other
Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                 29                          ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                              Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                             24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                         Initialization

                     IEEE1500 inputs (WRCK, SELECTWIR, SHIFTWR, CAPTUREWR, UPDATEWR, WSI) must
                     be driven per IEEE1500 Port Input and Output Timings figure at time tWINIT2 before WRST_n
                     is pulled HIGH (see IEEE1500 Test Port AC Timing Parameters). The CATTRIP output is
                     forced to LOW from the end of tINIT6 to the end of tINIT3 and is valid after tINIT3.
                5. While R[3:0] and C[2:0] remain driven to PDE and CNOP states as defined in step 4, the CK
                   clock shall be started and stable clocks shall be maintained for minimum of tINIT4 time before
                   R[3:0] is driven HIGH. Since R0 is a synchronous signal, the corresponding setup time to clock
                   (tIS) must be met. Also, RNOP and CNOP commands must be registered with tIS/tIH satisfied.
                   After R[3:0] are registered HIGH, a minimum tINIT5 time must be satisfied before issuing a first
                   MRS command. At or before the time that R[3:0] are driven HIGH, WDQS_t and WDQS_c must
                   be driven to LOW and HIGH static levels, respectively. A stable CK clock shall be maintained
                   except when a channel is in power-down or self refresh state. See Power-Down and Self




                                                                         A
                   Refresh sections for conditions about stopping and re-starting the CK clock.




                                                                        D
                A stable CK clock must be applied within 3 seconds after RESET_n was pulled HIGH. For debug
                purposes, the 1 minute and 3 second delay limits may be extended to 6 minutes each provided the


                                                                 rN
                device is operated in this debug mode for no more than 24 cumulative hours.
                6. Issue all MRS commands to configure the HBM3 DRAM appropriately for the application
                                                            de
                   setting.
                                                    un

                7. The HBM3 DRAM is now ready for normal operation.

Initialization Sequence with Stable Power
                 The following sequence must be satisfied to perform a functional reset when power is kept stable at
                 the HBM3 DRAM. See Figure 7.
                 1. RESET_n must be driven LOW anytime when a functional reset is needed. All other input
                    signals may be in an undefined state (driven LOW or HIGH, or High-Z) at this point except
                    WRST_n and CATTRIP as shown in Figure 7 . RESET_n must be maintained LOW for a
                    minimum of tPW_RESET.
                 2. A time tINIT2 before RESET_n is pulled HIGH, CK_t and CK_c must be driven to static LOW
                    and HIGH levels, respectively.
 Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
 Rev. L 06/2025                                                                     31                               ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                                    Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                                           24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                                       Initialization

                 3. R[3:0] must be driven to PDE state (HIGH, LOW, HIGH, LOW) and C[2:0] must be driven to
                    CNOP state (HIGH, HIGH, HIGH) a time tINIT7 before the CK clock is started. R[9:4] and C[7:3]
                    are allowed to remain in an undefined state. Alternately, the IEEE1500 port HBM_RESET
                    instruction may be used to perform a re-initialization, with RESET_n continuing to be driven
                    HIGH. Refer to the HBM_RESET Instruction section.
                 4. Follow steps 5 to 7 as described in section HBM3 Power-Up and Initialization Sequence. Note
                    that the CATTRIP output is not cleared by a functional reset.

Disable

                sequence.

                check for and correct failed connections on the row and column command buses, which must be
                correctly driven to RNOP and CNOP as part of the above initialization sequences. DWORD lane
                repairs are also allowed. The sequence may also be used to disable a faulty channel before normal
                operation mode is entered.

Clocking
                The HBM3 DRAM captures commands and addresses on the row and column buses using a
                differential clock CK_t/CK_c. Both buses operate at double data rate (DDR).
                The HBM DRAM has uni-directional differential write strobes (WDQS_t/WDQS_c) and read strobes
                (RDQS_t/RDQS_c).per 32 DQ (DWORD). The data bus operates at double data rate (DDR).

                The frequency of WDQS and RDQS strobes is nominally 2x the CK clock frequency. CK clock and
                WDQS are generated from the same clock source. The HBM3 DRAM generates the RDQS strobe
                from the incoming WDQS strobe.
                The WDQS frequency is internally divided by 2 to match the CK clock frequency. Four internal
                WDQS phases (0°, 90°, 180° and 270°) are generated for the 4 UI of write or read data per CK
                clock cycle as shown in Figure 11. The internal WDQS divider is reset at exit from reset state,
                power-down exit and self refresh exit.
                The sum of the WDQS pulses including pre- and postambles must be an even number for all write
                and read transactions such that the internal WDQS divider state is back at its reset state once the
                transaction has finished. With that, no specific synchronization between CK and WDQS is required.
                During idle states, WDQS_t and WDQS_c must be driven to LOW and HIGH static levels,




                                                                    A
                respectively, and the HBM3 DRAM drives RDQS_t and RDQS_c to LOW and HIGH static levels,




                                                                   D
                respectively. WDQS and RDQS preamble pulses are provided to reduce inter-symbol interference
                (ISI) at the receiver


                                                            rN
                During WDQS-to-CK alignment training, the WDQS phase shall be shifted against the CK clock
                phase to meet the tDQSS timing. See WDQS-to-CK Alignment Training for details.
                                                      de
                During WRITE data training for the unmatched DQ-to-WDQS path, the write data shall be shifted
                against the WDQS strobe while the CK and WDQS phases shall be kept stable.
                                                 un

                •    a rising CK (or WDQS, RDQS) edge is defined as the crossing of the rising edge of CK_t (or
                     WDQS_t, RDQS_t) and the falling edge of CK_c (or WDQS_c, RDQS_c);

Error Correction Code (ECC)
                 The HBM3 DRAM uses a symbol-based on-die error correction code (ECC), read/write meta-data
                 bits, an error scrubbing mechanism, an error transparency protocol, interface transmission parity,
                 and fault isolation limits to achieve a high level of system RAS.
                 32 bits of on-die ECC bits enable a single symbol correction scheme over 272-bit user data (256
                 bits of data and 16 bits of meta data). These 272 bits of user data are transmitted on write and read
                 transactions as a burst of eight via 32 DQ signals for data and 2 ECC signals for meta data. User
                 data and on-die ECC bits are stored together in the array as a 304-bit code-word. The on-die ECC
                 cannot be disabled.
                 An overview of the HBM3 on-die ECC engine is shown in Figure 13.




                                                                      A
                 Figure 13: On-Die ECC Overview




                                                                     D
                                                               rN
                                                   Data to Memory
                                                                                                 Code Word
                                                                                                 To Memory

                           No Error   Syndrome              Syndrome

                                  ov




                                           Error Magnitude
                                Pr




                                        Error
                     Corrected Data
                                      Correction


                 On writes the HBM3 DRAM computes the check bits and writes the data and check bits to the
                 array. On reads the HBM3 DRAM corrects all errors up to at least the single symbol size before
                 returning the data to the memory controller. The HBM3 DRAM does not write the corrected data
                 back to the memory array during a read cycle.
                 The transmission of meta data on the ECC signals can be disabled via the MD bit in MR9 OP0.
                 When MD is off, the ECC input receivers and output buffers are disabled. The meta data written to
                 the array are not specified, and any meta data read from the array are not transmitted. The DRAM
                 can only guarantee valid array meta data if written while the MD function is enabled. The basic
                 array write and read operations and the ECC engine’s operation are not affected by the MD bit.

Fault Isolation
                 Fault isolation is the management of errors caused by various faults to be isolated within certain
                 boundaries regardless of the on-die-ECC operation. The fault isolation boundaries have been
                 chosen in accordance with the ECC symbol size to maximize the correction capability of most
                 common multi-bit faults.

Error Correction Transparency
                The HBM3 device provides transparency of actions by the on-die ECC engine. The severity of an
                error denotes the outcome of the on-die ECC processing during a read operation. The error
                severity information is conveyed on the SEV signals along with the read data, if this error reporting
                is enabled by the SEVR bit in MR9 OP1. The severity is encoded for each read transaction as
                shown in Table 30. The SEV signals will be High-Z when the error severity reporting is disabled.
                A read transaction with a corrected single bit error (CEs) will be reported as error-free (NE) unless
                the error count (ERRCNT) maintained by the Error Check and Scrub (ECS) engine has exceeded
                the error threshold (ERRTH). Refer also to Figure 17 regarding error signaling on SEV outputs.

                Table 30: Error Severity Encoding on SEV Signals for Reads

ECC Engine Test Mode
                The HBM3 DRAM provides a test mode for the ECC error correction engine that enables a health
                                               ed



                check of this logic without accessing the memory array as illustrated in Figure 14. The test mode is
                controlled by bits in MR9 OP[3:2].
                                   id




                The test mode utilizes the regular data interface (DQ, ECC) and regular WRITE and READ
                                 ov




                commands to write an error vector to a DRAM internal register and read back the corrected error
                vector from that register and associated error severity information.
                               Pr




                While in this test mode the ECC engine will not calculate check bits (OD-ECC bits) from the write
                data but instead assume one of two hard-coded check bit words CW0 (all 0s) or CW1 (all 1s) as
                selected by bit in MR9 OP3. On a READ the ECC engine will correct the data word based on the
                selected check bit word.
                WRITE and READ commands can be issued without preceding ACTIVATE command, leaving the
                memory array in bank idle state. No commands other than RNOP, CNOP, WRITE, READ and MRS
                to disable this test mode are allowed while this test mode is active.

Error Check and Scrub (ECS)
                The HBM3 DRAM implements an ECC error check and scrub (ECS) mode with an error counting
                scheme for transparency. Five mode register bits control ECS operation:
                                                              de
                Table 32: Error Check and Scrub (ECS) Related Mode Registers
                                                       un

                 Mode Register                                                  Purpose
                 MR9 OP4               Controls the repurposing of REFab commands for ECS during normal operation
                                               ed



                 (ECSREF)
                 MR9 OP5               Controls ECS operation during self refresh
                                   id




                 (ECSSRF)
                                 ov




                 MR9 OP6               Controls whether a code-word will be corrected and written back to the memory array in
                 (ECSCEM)              case of a correctable multi-bit error
                               Pr




                 MR9 OP7               Resets the ECS error type and address log for both PCs. This bit is self-clearing
                 (ECSRES)              meaning that it automatically returns back to the 0B value after the reset function has
                                       been issued. The bit does not reset the internal ECS address counter for ECS operation
                 MR8 OP2               Controls the ECS error type and address log auto reset upon a read (CaptureWR event)
                 (ECSLOG)
                Note:      1. See also Table 19 and Table 20 for MR8 and MR9 details.

                ECS will operate in the background during REFab and self refresh periods when ECS is enabled
                by the ECSREF and ECSSRF bits, respectively. It allows the HBM3 DRAM to internally detect
                errors and write the corrected data back to the array (scrub errors) while providing transparency.
                Errors corrected during ECS cycles are logged in the transparency registers as outlined below.
                ECS is disabled by default. The HBM3 DRAM must have all array bits written prior to enabling ECS
                operations to avoid generating false failures. It is recommended that a full error scrub of the array is
                performed at least once every 24 hours (tECS).
                ECS modes in MR9 OP[6:4] shall be programmed during initialization and shall not be changed
                once the first ECS operation occurs unless followed by a device reset or an ECS error type and
                address reset (MR9 OP7), otherwise an unknown operation could result during subsequent ECS
                operations.

                ECS can be disabled by setting both bits MR9 OP[5:4] back to 00B. Disabling ECS does not reset
                the ECS error type and address log, nor does it reset the internal ECS error counter (ERRCNT, see
                below).
                During each single auto ECS operation, the HBM3 DRAM generates the following internally self-
                timed command sequence: ACTIVATE – READ – WRITE – PRECHARGE. This internal read-
                modify-write cycle will:
                1. read one entire code-word from the array;
                2. check the code-word for errors;
                3. write the corrected code-word back to the array in case a single-bit error (CEs) was detected;
                4. write the corrected code-word back to the array in case a multi-bit error (CEm) was detected




                                                                          A
                   and correction of multi-bit errors is enabled via the ECSCEM bit;




                                                                         D
                5. not write any data back to the array in case the error is uncorrectable (UE).



                                                                  rN
                After each ECS operation, the internal ECS address counter increments the column address such
                that the next column address (code-word and check bits) is selected. Once the column counter
                wraps (all columns on a row have been accessed), the row counter will increment until all rows
                                                              de
                within a bank are accessed. When the row counter wraps (all rows within the bank have been
                accessed), the bank counter will increment until all banks within one SID have been accessed. In
                                                        un

                that case all counter wrap to 0, equivalent to the completion of one tECS period.
                Error scrubbing is performed simultaneously on all SID and logged separately per SID.
                                                ed



                The ECS operation timing is shown in Figure 16. The maximum spacing between REFab
                commands to complete the scrub within the recommended 24 hours is tECSint as outlined in Table
                                   id




                33. Meeting this requirement allows the DRAM to perform the ECS operations without placing
                                 ov




                additional restrictions on refresh mode usage, i.e. all-bank / per-bank refresh. The ECS operation
                with REFab must be scheduled separately for PC0 and PC1 by issuing REFab commands evenly
                to PC0 and PC1. REFab commands issued in excess of required by the DRAM for ECS operations
                               Pr




                (one REFab per tECSint) may be used by the DRAM for normal refresh operation.
                The HBM3 DRAM performs ECS operations while in self refresh mode if this function is enabled by
                the ECSSRF bit. These ECS operations occur approximately at tECSint spacing in order to
                generate the same scrubbing rate as recommended with REFab commands. However, some
                variation in the scrubbing rate may be encountered while in self refresh since the DRAM will need
                to synchronize the internal operations to an internal oscillator. Entering and exiting self refresh will
                not reset the ECS error log registers. All timings for the maximum spacing between REFab
                commands or another self refresh entry are allowed to restart upon self refresh exit.

Data Bus Inversion (DBIac)
                HBM3 DRAMs supports a byte granular Data Bus Inversion (DBIac). The corresponding DBI signal
                is a DDR I/O and driven or sampled along with the DQs for read and write operations.
                The word DBI refers to the internal state of the device unless explicitly noted as DBI signal. The
                DBIac function can be enabled or disabled independently for writes per MR0 OP1 (WDBI) and for
                reads per MR0 OP0 (RDBI).
                The DBI input is a don’t care and the DBI input receivers are disabled when WDBI is disabled. The
                DBI output buffers are turned off when RDBI is disabled.

                Figure 18: DBIac Algorithm

                Write operation: the HBM3 DRAM inverts write data received on the DQ inputs in case DBI is
                sampled HIGH or leaves the write data non-inverted in case DBI is sampled LOW. Note that the
                ECC inputs are not affected by the DBIac function.
                Read operation: the HBM3 DRAM counts the number of DQ signals that are transitioning from the
                previous state. Note that the ECC and SEV outputs are not affected by DBIac. See Internal DBIac
                States with Read for bus pre-conditioning. The HBM3 DRAM inverts read data and sets DBI HIGH
                when the number of changing data bits within a byte is greater than 4, or when the number of
                changing data bits within a byte equals 4 and DBI was HIGH; otherwise the HBM3 DRAM does not
                invert the read data and sets DBI LOW.

Command/Address Parity
                The HBM3 DRAM includes a command/address parity checking function controlled by the CAPAR
                bit in MR0 OP6. The function is disabled by default. The APAR input and AERR output are
                associated with the function. APAR is enabled only when the function is enabled.
                If enabled, the parity is calculated every CK clock cycle separately on both the rising and falling CK
                clock edges over input signals R[9:0], C[7:0], ARFU and APAR as summarized in Table 36. The
                AERR output indicates whether a parity error has occurred or not on either the rising or falling CK
                clock edge (or both edges). The HBM3 DRAM executes commands regardless of a
                command/address parity error.

                Table 36: Command/Address Parity Function Table
                                       Inputs                                  Sum of Inputs Received HIGH                          AERR
                                                                                              Even                                   LOW
                        R[9:0], C[7:0], ARFU, APAR
                                                                                              Odd                                   HIGH
                Note:      1. See Command Truth Tables for command and device state exceptions.

                The HBM3 DRAM may begin to check parity on the next clock cycle following the MODE
                REGISTER SET command that enables the parity checking function; it will have the parity check
                enabled latest when tMOD has expired after that MODE REGISTER SET command. The HBM3
                DRAM therefore requires all subsequent commands including RNOP and CNOP to be issued with
                correct parity until when tMOD has expired for the MODE REGISTER SET command that disables
                the parity calculation. See also the Power-Down and Self Refresh sections. AERR is driven LOW
                by the HBM3 DRAM at reset.
                For every parity error, AERR is driven HIGH for 1 tCK, tPARAC after the corresponding cycle of the
                error inputs. In the case of consecutive errors, the AERR signal will stay HIGH during the next
                cycle. The parity function should not be disabled within tPARAC after an access command.

Data Parity
                The HBM3 DRAM includes a data parity checking function for writes controlled by the WPAR bit in
                MR0 OP5, and a data parity generation function for reads controlled by the RPAR bit in MR0 OP4.
                Both WPAR and RPAR functions are disabled by default. There is one DPAR bidirectional DDR I/O
                and one DERR output signal per DWORD associated with the function. The DPAR input is enabled
                with WPAR during writes, and the DPAR output is enabled with RPAR during reads, otherwise
                DPAR is disabled.
                The data parity function includes a programmable parity latency PL between the corresponding
                data and the DPAR signal. PL is programmed in MR1 OP[7:5] and is the same for writes and
                reads. The corresponding DPAR signal will be received and sent PL cycles later. The WDQS and
                RDQS strobes will have additional strobe cycles with the same preamble and postamble to




                                                                       A
                accommodate the latching of the delayed DPAR signal at both ends. Examples of reads and writes
                with DQ parity enabled can be found in the Write Command and Read Command sections.




                                                                      D
                On read transactions, the HBM generates parity and transmits the parity on the DPAR signal along


                                                              rN
                with the corresponding data on DQ, DBI and ECC.
                On write transactions, the HBM3 DRAM compares the DPAR input with the corresponding data
                                                        de
                received on DQ, DBI and ECC inputs as summarized in Table 37. The parity calculation is
                performed separately for each UI of a write burst.
                                                  un

                If an error occurs in any single or in multiple UIs within one clock cycle of a write burst (D0 ... D3 or
                D4 ... D7), DERR is driven HIGH for 1 tCK tPARDQ after the corresponding cycle of error inputs.
                The tPARDQ interval for errors occurring during the first clock cycle of a write burst begins (WL +
                                          ed



                PL) clock cycles after the WRITE command was issued. In case of errors within the first and the
                second clock cycle of a write burst, DERR will stay HIGH during the next cycle. DERR is driven
                                   id




                LOW by the HBM3 DRAM at reset.
                                 ov




                When an error occurs, the HBM3 DRAM does not block the write data. The HBM3 DRAM
                completes the write transaction to the array as normal.
                               Pr




                WPAR should not be disabled within (WL + PL+ 1 tCK + tPARDQ) after the WRITE command in
                order to not create a conflict with any ongoing parity operation. For the same reason RPAR should
                not be disabled within tRDMRS after the READ command.
                As outlined in Table 37, meta data received and sent via the ECC signals are included in the parity
                check and parity generation only when these signals are enabled by the MD bit in MR9 OP0.
                Similarly, the DBI signals are included in the parity check and parity generation only when these
                signals are enabled by the WDBI and RDBI bits in MR0 OP[1:0]. The SEV signals are not included
                in the parity check or parity generation.

ACTIVATE Command (ACT)
                Before a READ or WRITE command can be issued to a bank, a row in that bank must be opened.
                This is accomplished via the ACTIVATE command, which selects the SID, bank and row to be
                activated. Once a row is open, a READ or WRITE command could be issued to that row, subject to
                the tRCD specification.
                The ACTIVATE command is a one-and-a-half-cycle command received on the row command
                inputs R[9:0] and latched with the rising and falling CK clock edges as shown in Figure 26. The
                command must be followed either by RNOP, PRECHARGE or PRECHARGE ALL on the falling CK
                clock edge of the second clock cycle. Note that a PRECHARGE ALL in that case must be for the
                other pseudo channel. A PRECHARGE command could be to any bank in the other pseudo
                channel as well as to a different bank in the same pseudo channel. In all cases the timing




                                                                              A
                requirements for issuing these commands must be met.




                                                                             D
                The actual bank and row activation is initiated with the second rising CK clock edge of the
                ACTIVATE command; therefore, all relevant timing parameters refer to this second rising CK clock


                                                                     rN
                edge as shown in subsequent timing diagrams.

Bank Restrictions
                There is a need to limit the number of bank activations in a rolling window to ensure that the
                instantaneous current supplying capability of the device is not exceeded. To reflect the short-term
                current supply capability, the parameter tFAW (four activate window) is defined: no more than 4
                banks may be activated in a rolling tFAW window. Converting to clocks is done by dividing tFAW
                (ns) by tCK (ns) and rounding up to next integer value. As an example of the rolling window, if
                (tFAW/tCK) rounds up to 25 clocks, and an ACTIVATE command is issued at clock T0, no more
                than three further ACTIVATE commands may be issued at clocks T1 through T24 as illustrated in
                Figure 28.

                PRECHARGE command issued to the bank.

Auto Precharge
                Auto precharge is a feature which performs the same individual bank precharge function described
                above, but without requiring an explicit PRECHARGE command. Auto precharge is nonpersistent
                meaning that it is enabled or disabled along for each individual READ or WRITE command.
                For read bursts an auto precharge of the bank and row that is addressed with the READ command
                begins RTP clock cycles after the READ command was issued or after RAS has been met, with
                RTP as programmed in clock cycles in MR5 OP[3:0] and RAS as programmed in clock cycles in
                MR4 OP[7:0].
                For write bursts an auto precharge of the bank and row that is addressed with the WRITE
                command begins (WL + 2 + WR) clock cycles after the WRITE command was issued or after RAS
                has been met, with WR as programmed in clock cycles in MR3 OP[7:0] and RAS as programmed
                in clock cycles in MR4 OP[7:0].
                Auto precharge ensures that the precharge is initiated at the earliest valid stage within a burst. The
                user must not issue another command to the same bank until the precharge (tRP) is completed.
Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                       60                    ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                                 Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                                 24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                               Operation

                This is determined as if an explicit PRECHARGE command was issued at the earliest possible
                time, as described for READ or WRITE commands. A precharge resulting from a READ or WRITE
                with auto precharge may occur in parallel with an explicit PRECHARGE (or PRECHARGE ALL)
                command. It is pointed out that an auto precharge is internally always issued with a rising CK clock
                edge, while explicit PRECHARGE (or PRECHARGE ALL) commands are supported on both clock
                edges.

Rounding Rules for Row Access Timings
                The HBM3 DRAM allows the PRECHARGE (PREpb) and PRECHARGE ALL (PREab) commands
                               Pr




                to be issued on both rising and falling CK clock edges, as e.g. illustrated in the Bank and Row
                Activation Command Cycle figure. To let a system take advantage of this flexibility in command
                scheduling, it is required to adapt the rounding rules for related row access timings.
                Traditionally, basic row access timings are converted into clock cycles using the formula NXX =
                RU(tXX/tCK), with XX representing either RAS, RTP, WR or RP parameters. This formula rounds
                the analog timings up to the next integer such that the subsequent command can be issued on the
                next rising clock edge that meets the analog value.
                For HBM3 DRAM, this formula is replaced by NXX = 0.5 × RU(2 × tXX/tCK), which rounds analog
                timings to the next rising or following clock edge that meets the analog value. The result may be
                the same as with the traditional formula, or 0.5 nCK less. The formula may be applied to row
                timings tRAS, tRTP, tWR and tRP only. If rounding the tRP timing results in a falling clock edge as
                the command slot for a subsequent row access command, it is required to add 0.5nCK to the result
                because all row commands following a row precharge can be issued on a rising clock edge only.
                Examples:
                1. tRAS = 33ns, tCK = 0.7ns; NRAS = 0.5 × RU(2 × tRAS/tCK) = 0.5 × RU(2 × 33/0.7) = 0.5 ×
                   RU(94.29) = 47.5.
                   Conclusion: when the ACTIVATE command was issued at T0, the earliest possible slot for a
                   PRECHARGE command is at T47.5 (falling clock edge).

Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                        62                                  ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                                Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                       24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                     Operation

                2. tRP = 15ns, tCK = 0.7ns; NRP = 0.5 × RU(2 × tRP/tCK) = 0.5 × RU(2 × 15/0.7) =
                   0.5 × RU(42.85) = 21.5.
                   Conclusion: when the PRECHARGE command was issued at T0 (rising edge), the earliest
                   possible slot for a subsequent ACTIVATE command is at T22, because the falling edge at
                   T21.5 is not supported for an ACVIVATE command and 0.5nCK must be added to the result.
                   However, when the PRECHARGE command was issued at T0.5 (falling edge), the earliest
                   possible slot for a subsequent ACTIVATE command is again at T22.

                                                                                A

                                               ed



                the REFRESH command.
                                   id

                “Don’t Care” during a REFRESH command.

PER-BANK REFRESH Command (REFpb)
                 The PER-BANK REFRESH command (REFpb) provides an alternative solution for the refresh of
                 the HBM3 device. The command initiates a refresh cycle on a single bank while accesses to other
                 banks including writes and reads are not affected. PER-BANK REFRESH is a half-cycle command
                 received on the row command inputs R[9:0] and latched with the rising CK clock edge as shown in
                 Figure 34. The command must be followed either by RNOP, PRECHARGE or PRECHARGE ALL
                 on the falling CK clock edge of the same cycle. Note that a PRECHARGE ALL must be for the
                 other pseudo channel. A PRECHARGE command could be to any bank in the other pseudo

                channel as well as to a different bank in the same pseudo channel. In all cases the timing

                The PER-BANK REFRESH command is nonpersistent, so it must be issued each time a refresh is
                required. A minimum time tRRD is required between an ACTIVATE command and a PER-BANK
                               Pr




                REFRESH command to a different bank. A minimum time tRREFD is required between any two
                PER-BANK REFRESH commands (see below for an exception requiring tRFCpb), and between a
                PER-BANK REFRESH command and an ACTIVATE command to a different bank as shown in
                Figure 35. A minimum time tRFCpb is required between a PER-BANK REFRESH command and an
                access command to the same bank that follows. The bank to be refreshed must be precharged
                with tRP satisfied prior to the PER-BANK REFRESH command. The bank is in idle state after
                completion of the PER-BANK REFRESH command.
                The row address for each bank is provided by internal refresh counters. This makes the row
                address bits “Don’t Care” during PER-BANK REFRESH commands.
                Rules for issuing PER-BANK REFRESH commands to the banks apply to each SID individually. A
                PER-BANK REFRESH command to one of the 16 banks per SID can be issued in any order. After
                all banks within an SID have been refreshed using the PER-BANK REFRESH command and after
                waiting for at least tRFCpb, the internal refresh counter is incremented and the controller can issue
                another set of PER-BANK REFRESH commands in the same or a different order. However, it is
                illegal to send another PER-BANK REFRESH command to a bank unless all banks within an SID
                have been refreshed using the PER-BANK REFRESH command. The controller must track the
                bank being refreshed by the PER-BANK REFRESH command.

Refresh Management (RFM)
                Periods of high DRAM activity may require additional refresh commands to protect the integrity of
                the stored data. The requirement for additional Refresh Management (RFM) is indicated in the
                RFM field of the DEVICE_ID WDR (see Table 90): RFM = 0B indicates that no additional refresh is
                needed beyond the refreshes specified in the REFRESH section of the specification; RFM = 1B
                indicates additional DRAM refresh management is required.




                                                                              A
                A suggested implementation of refresh management by the controller monitors ACTIVATE
                commands issued per bank to the device. This activity can be monitored as a rolling accumulated




                                                                             D
                ACTIVATE (RAA) count. Each ACTIVATE command will increment the RAA count by 1 for the



                                                                     rN
                individual bank receiving the ACTIVATE command.
                When the RAA count reaches a DRAM vendor specified Initial Management Threshold (RAAIMT),
                                                              de
                which is indicated by the HBM3 DRAM in the RAAIMT field of the DEVICE_ID WDR, additional
                refresh management is needed. Executing a refresh management command allows additional time
                                                        un

                for the HBM3 DRAM to manage refresh internally. The RFM operation can be initiated to all banks
                with the (all-bank) REFRESH MANAGEMENT (RFMab) command, or to a single bank with the
                PER-BANK REFRESH MANAGEMENT (RFMpb) command. The encoding of RFM related
                                               ed



                commands RFMab and RFMpb is shown in Figure 37.

                Figure 37: REFRESH MANAGEMENT and PER-BANK REFRESH MANAGEMENT Commands

                Both half-cycle commands are received on the R[9:0] inputs and latched with the rising CK clock
                edge. They must be followed either by RNOP, PRECHARGE or PRECHARGE ALL on the falling
                CK clock edge of the same cycle. Note that a PRECHARGE ALL must be for the other pseudo
                channel. In case of a PER-BANK REFRESH MANAGEMENT command a PRECHARGE command
                could be to any bank in the other pseudo channel as well as to a different bank in the same pseudo
                channel. In all cases the timing requirements for issuing these commands must be met.
                Parity is evaluated with the REFRESH MANAGEMENT and PER-BANK REFRESH
                MANAGEMENT commands when CA parity is enabled in MR0 OP6.
                An HBM3 DRAM not requiring refresh management will ignore RFMab and RFMpb commands and
                execute an RNOP command instead.
                The REFRESH MANAGEMENT and PER-BANK REFRESH MANAGEMENT command scheduling




                                                                   A
                shall meet the same minimum separation requirements as those for the REFRESH and PER-BANK




                                                                  D
                REFRESH commands, respectively (see REFRESH Command (REFab) and PER-BANK
                REFRESH Command (REFpb) sections). The REFRESH MANAGEMENT command period is the


                                                           rN
                same as the REFRESH command period (tRFCab), and the PER-BANK REFRESH
                MANAGEMENT command period is the same as the PER-BANK REFRESH command period
                                                     de
                (tRFCpb). The requirement for PER-BANK REFRESH commands to be issued to all banks in a
                rolling fashion does not apply to PER-BANK REFRESH MANAGEMENT commands.
                                               un

                When an RFM command is issued to the HBM3 DRAM, the RAA counter in any bank receiving the
                command can be decremented by the RAAIMT value, down to a minimum RAA value of 0 (no
                negative or “pull-in” of RFM commands is allowed). Issuing an RFMab command allows the RAA
                                        ed



                count in all banks to be decremented by the RAAIMT value. Issuing an RFMpb command allows
                the RAA count only in the bank selected by {SID[1:0], BA[3:0]} to be decremented by the RAAIMT
                                   id




                value.
                                 ov




                RFM commands are allowed to accumulate or “postpone”, but the RAA counter shall never exceed
                a vendor specified RAA Maximum Management Threshold (RAAMMT), which is indicated by the
                               Pr




                HBM3 DRAM in the RAAMMT field of the DEVICE_ID WDR (see Table 90). If the RAA counter
                reaches RAAMMT, no additional ACTIVATE commands are allowed to the bank until one or more
                REF or RFM commands have been issued to reduce the RAA counter below the maximum value.
                An RFM command does not replace the requirement for the controller to issue periodic REF
                commands to the HBM3 DRAM, nor does an RFM command affect internal refresh counters. The
                RFM commands are bonus time for the HBM3 DRAM to manage refresh internally. However,
                issuing a REF command also allows decrementing the RAA counter by a value indicated the
                RAA_CNT_DEC field of the DEVICE_ID WDR. Hence, any periodic REF command issued to the
                HBM3 DRAM allows the RAA counter of the banks being refreshed to be decremented by that
                value. Issuing an REFab command allows the RAA count in all banks to be decremented by that
                value. Issuing an REFpb command allows the RAA count only in the bank selected by {SID[1:0],
                BA[3:0]} to be decremented by that value.
                The per-bank RAA count values may be reset to 0 when the HBM3 DRAM is held in self refresh for
                at least tRAASRF time. No decrement to the per-bank RAA count values is allowed for entering or
                exiting self refresh and when the HBM3 DRAM is held in self refresh for less than tRAASRF time.

Adaptive Refresh Management (ARFM)
                 This HBM3 DRAM supports a refresh management mode called Adaptive Refresh Management
                 (ARFM). The HBM3 DRAM indicates the support of ARFM via the ARFM bit in the IEEE1500
                 DEVICE_ID WDR. Since RFM related parameters RAAIMT, RAAMMT and RAADEC are read-only,
                 the ARFM mode allows the controller flexibility to choose additional (lower) RFM threshold settings
                 called “RFM levels”. The RFM levels permit alignment of the controller issued RFM commands with
                 the DRAM internal management of these commands. MR8 OP[5:4] select the RFM level as shown
                 in in Table 44.

                                                              de
      11                 Level C          RFM is required     RAAIMT_C        RAAMMT_C             RAADEC_C
                 Notes:     1. RAAIMT, RAAMMT and RAADEC values are set by DRAM vendor in the IEEE1500 DEVICE_ID WDR.
                                                        un

                 The Adaptive RFM mode inherits the RAA counting and decrement attributes of the standard RFM
                 mode, while using the alternate RAAIMT, RAAMMT and RAADEC values for the selected RFM
                                                ed



                 level. Increasing the RFM level results in increased need for RFM commands. Level C is highest
                 RFM level. The alternate RAAIMT, RAAMMT and RAADEC values for RFM level A to C can be
                                    id

                                  ov

                 with RFM or pending REF commands, prior to making a change to the ARFM level.
                                Pr

                 DEVICE_ID WDR = 0) to override that initial setting and enable RFM by programming a non-

Column No Operation Command (CNOP)
                The COLUMN NO OPERATION (CNOP) command is a 1-cycle command as shown in Figure 38
                and is used to instruct the HBM3 DRAM to perform a NOP as the column command; this prevents
                unwanted column commands from being registered during idle or wait states. Operations already in
                progress are not affected.
                Parity is evaluated with the CNOP command when CA parity is enabled in MR0 OP6.

Mode Register Set Command (MRS)
                                 ov




                MODE REGISTER SET is a one-cycle command received on the column command inputs C[7:0]
                               Pr




                and latched with the rising and falling CK clock edges. The command requires an RNOP command
                on the row command inputs R[9:0].
                The command is used to load the mode registers of the HBM3 DRAM. Inputs MA[4:0] select one of
                the sixteen mode registers, and the inputs OP[7:0] determine the opcode to be loaded as shown in
                Figure 39. Refer to the mode register section for the register definition.
                The MODE REGISTER SET (MRS) command can only be issued when all banks are idle, the time
                t
                 RDMRS from a preceding READ command has elapsed and the time tWRMRS from a preceding
                WRITE command has elapsed. The MRS command cycle time tMRD is required to complete the
                write operation to the mode register and is the minimum time required between two MRS
                commands. The MRS command to Non-MRS command delay, tMOD, is required by the HBM3
                DRAM to update the features, and is the minimum time required from an MRS command to a non-
                MRS command excluding RNOP and CNOP.
                Parity is evaluated with the MODE REGISTER SET command when CA parity has already been
                enabled in MR0 OP6 prior to this MODE REGISTER SET command. When CA parity is enabled by
                a MODE REGISTER SET command, the HBM3 DRAM requires all subsequent commands
                including RNOP and CNOP to be issued with correct parity until tMOD has expired for the MODE
                REGISTER SET command that disables CA parity. See Figure 20 for enabling and disabling CA
                parity.

WRITE Command (WR/WRA)
                A write burst is initiated with a WRITE command. WRITE is a one-cycle command received on the
                column command inputs C[7:0] and latched with the rising and falling CK clock edges as shown in
                Figure 41. The SID, bank and column addresses are provided with the WRITE command, and auto
                precharge is either enabled or disabled for that access.
                Parity is evaluated with the WRITE command when CA parity is enabled in MR0 OP6.

                Figure 41: WRITE Command

                CK_c
                CK_t




                                                                            A
                C0                              BA1




                                                                           D
                C1                              BA2

                C2                              BA3
                                                                    rN
                                                             de
                                   EN AP
                C3                              CA0
                                                      un

                                   DIS AP
                C4                  PC          CA1
                                              ed

                                   id




                C6                 SID1/V       CA3
                                 ov




                C7                  BA0         CA4
                               Pr




                Note:      1. PC = Pseudo Channel 0 or 1; SID = Stack ID; BA = Bank address; CA = Column address;
                              V = Valid (H or L); EN AP = Enable auto precharge; DIS AP = Disable auto precharge

                The length of the burst initiated with a WRITE command is eight, and the column address is unique
                for this burst of eight. There is no interruption nor truncation of write bursts.
                The write latency (WL) is defined from the rising CK edge on which the WRITE command is issued
                to the rising CK edge from which the tDQSS delay is measured, with the number of clock cycles as
                programmed in the WL field of MR1.
                The write data strobe for a write burst must include two WDQS preamble pulses and two WDQS
                postamble pulses. The first WDQS edge must be driven (WL-1) × tCK + tDQSS after the rising CK
                edge when the WRITE command was issued.
                The HBM3 DRAM uses an un-matched WDQS-to-data path to achieve lower power consumption.
                The write data (DQ, DBI, ECC) must arrive center-aligned to the internal latching clock a time
                t
                 WDQS2DQ_I after the corresponding WDQS edges. tWDQS2DQ_I is the WDQS-to-DQ/DBI/ECC
                offset; the offset varies with PVT and must be trained prior to any write operation.
                The first valid write data must arrive (WL × tCK + tDQSS + tWDQS2DQ_I) after the rising CK edge
                when the WRITE command was issued. Each subsequent write data must be applied nominally
                t
                 CK/4 later and will be latched with subsequent WDQS edges.

Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                      74                               ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.

                                                                                           24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                         Operation

                The internal WDQS clock tree is optimized for lowest signal skew among signals within a group as
                outlined in Table 46. The grouping is aligned with the physical location of signals in a DWORD (see
                HBM3 microbump matrix) with no lane being repaired.
                Each group contains 5 to 8 signals. The internal WDQS clock tree however compensates the
                different loading by e.g. adding dummy loads. The per-group de-skew is also deterministic and not
                frequency dependent. A larger signal skew should be expected between different groups. A per-
                group de-skew is recommended to achieve the largest signaling margin for write data.

                 Data from any write burst may be concatenated with data from a subsequent WRITE command. A
                 continuous flow of data can be maintained as shown in Figure 45. The first data element from the
                 new burst follows the last element of a completed burst. The new WRITE command should be
                 issued after the previous WRITE command according to the tCCDS timing. If that WRITE command
                 is to another idle bank then an ACTIVATE command must precede the WRITE command and
                 t
                  RCDWR also must be met.

                 A READ can be issued any time after a WRITE command as long as the bus turnaround time tWTR
                 is met as shown in Figure 47. If that READ command is to another idle bank, then an ACTIVATE
                 command must precede the READ command and tRCDRD also must be met.
                 The data bus is preconditioned for the first read burst by being driven LOW one clock cycles (even
                 bytes) and half a clock cycle (odd bytes) prior to the first valid data element of the read burst
                 regardless of whether RDBI is enabled in MR0 or not.
                 Four WDQS preambles pulses are received at Ta+8 and Ta+9, and two RDQS preamble pulses
                 are returned at Ta+9. Two WDQS postamble pulses are received and two RDQS postamble pulses
                 are returned at Ta+12.

READ Command (RD/RDA)
                                    id




                 A read burst is initiated with a READ command. READ is a one-cycle command received on the
                 column command inputs C[7:0] and latched with the rising and falling CK clock edges as shown in
                                  ov




                 Figure 49. The SID, bank and column addresses are provided with the READ command, and auto
                 precharge is either enabled or disabled for that access.
                                Pr




                 Parity is evaluated with the READ command when CA parity is enabled in MR0 OP6.
                 The length of the burst initiated with a READ command is eight, and the column address is unique
                 for this burst of eight. There is no interruption nor truncation of read bursts.
                 The read latency (RL) is defined from the rising CK edge on which the READ command is issued to
                 the rising CK edge from which the tDQSS delay is measured, with the number of clock cycles as
                 programmed in the RL field of MR2. The first valid data is available (RL × tCK + tDQSS +
                 t
                  WDQS2DQ_O) after the rising CK edge when the READ command was issued.
                 The write data strobe (WDQS) is the clock source for read data (DQ, DBI, ECC, SEV) and the read
                 data strobe (RDQS). WDQS must meet the same tDQSS timing relative to the CK clock as for
                 writes.
                 The write data strobe for a read burst must include four WDQS preamble pulses and two WDQS
                 postamble pulses; the first WDQS edge must be driven ((RL-2) × tCK + tDQSS) after the rising CK
                 edge when the READ command was issued.

                the rising CK edge when the READ command was issued. Each subsequent data-out is driven
                nominally tCK/4 later.
                The output drivers are enabled and begin driving either HIGH or LOW nominally two WDQS cycles
                (odd bytes) and one WDQS cycle (even bytes) prior to the first valid data bit. See Internal DBIac
                States with Read for bus pre-conditioning with RDBI enabled and disabled modes on a first READ
                command.
                The output drivers will drive High-Z after the completion of the burst provided no other READ
                command has been issued.
                The internal WDQS clock tree is optimized for lowest signal skew among signals within a group as
                outlined in Table 47. The grouping is aligned with the physical location of signals in a DWORD (see
                HBM3 microbump matrix) with no lane being repaired.
                Each group contains 6 to 8 signals. The internal WDQS clock tree however compensates the
                different loading by e.g. adding dummy loads. The per-group de-skew is also deterministic and not
                frequency dependent. A larger signal skew should be expected between different groups. A per-
                group de-skew is recommended to achieve the largest signaling margin for read data.
                In this context RDQS_t and RDQS_c are treated as regular data out signals within group T4.

Internal DBIac State with Read
                                 ov




                The HBM3 DRAM resets the internal DBIac state to LOW whenever any of the following events
                               Pr




                occur:
                •    RESET_n de-assertion;
                •    a MODE REGISTER SET (MRS) command is received, or the mode registers have been
                     updated via the IEEE1500 MODE_REGISTER_DUMP_SET instruction;
                •    a write-to-read bus turnaround;
                •    self refresh exit.
                For all other events or commands, the internal DBIac state is not reset and the HBM3 DRAM will
                use its previous state for DBIac calculation.
                When a first READ command is registered after a DBI reset, the HBM3 DRAM preconditions the
                bus to LOW prior to read data regardless whether RDBI is enabled or disabled in the mode
                register, as shown in Figure 58 in case of a write-to-read bus turnaround. The internal state D7
                corresponding to the last UI of the read burst is internally stored as a seed value for a subsequent
                read burst.
                The DPAR signal is not included in the DBI calculation and not preconditioned to LOW; its initial
                state is undefined (LOW or HIGH).

Power-Down
                Power-down is entered with the POWER-DOWN ENTRY command. POWER-DOWN ENTRY is a
                one-cycle command received on the row command inputs R[9:0] and latched with the rising and
                falling CK clock edges as shown in Figure 60. The command requires a CNOP command on the
                column command inputs C[7:0].

                Figure 60: POWER_DOWN ENTRY Command

                CK_c
                CK_t
                R0




                                                                            A
                R1




                                                                           D
                                                                    rN
                R2

                R3
                                                              de
                R[9:4]             V                V
                                                         un

                Note:      1. V = Valid (H or L)
                                                   ed



                Power-down entry must not be issued when read or write operations are in progress on either PC.
                A read operation is completed when the last data element including parity (when enabled) and
                                   id




                RDQS postamble have been transmitted on the outputs. A write operation is completed when the
                last data element including parity (when enabled) has been written to the memory array with tWR
                                 ov




                satisfied; for writes with auto-precharge, the number of clock cycles programmed in the mode
                register for WR must have elapsed instead.
                               Pr




                Power-down entry is allowed while any other operations such as row activation, precharge, auto
                precharge, or refresh are in progress, but the power-down IDD specification will not apply until such
                operations are complete.
                If power-down occurs when all banks are idle, this mode is referred to as precharge power-down; if
                power-down occurs when there is a row active in any bank, this mode is referred to as active
                power-down.
                To ensure that there is enough time to internally process the power-down entry, POWER-DOWN
                ENTRY and CNOP commands have to be maintained for tCPDED period. Also, the CK clock must
                be held stable for tCKPDE cycles.
                Once tCPDED and tCKPDE have been met, the signals shall have the following states (see Table
                48):
                •    The R0 input receivers remains active, and R0 = LOW must be maintained to keep the HBM3
                     DRAM in power-down;
                •    The CK clock receiver remains active. The clock may be stopped with CK_t and CK_c being
                     driven to static LOW and HIGH levels, respectively; in that case the clock must be stable again
                     with tCH(min) and tCL(min) satisfied at least tCKPDX cycles prior to power-down exit;
                •    RDQS_t and RDQS_c continue driving static LOW and HIGH levels, respectively;

Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                      94                     ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                                Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                                     24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                                   Operation

                •     AERR, DERR continue driving static LOW levels;
                •     TEMP and CATTRIP continue driving valid HIGH or LOW levels
                •     All other input and output buffers are deactivated.

                                                              de
                No refresh operations are performed in power-down mode. The maximum duration in power-down
                mode is limited by the refresh requirements of the device.

                While in power-down the device will maintain the internal DBI state for the DBIac calculation when
                DBI is enabled in the mode register.
                                               ed

                                 ov




                If CA parity is enabled in MR0 OP6, parity is evaluated for the POWER-DOWN ENTRY command.
                The HBM3 DRAM requires POWER-DOWN ENTRY, RNOP and CNOP commands with valid
                parity for the entire tCPDED period, while it will suspend parity checking after power-down entry
                               Pr




                and drive AERR to a static LOW. DERR remains LOW as there are no data bursts in progress at
                this time.
                Parity is not evaluated for the POWER-DOWN EXIT command. The HBM3 DRAM requires RNOP
                and CNOP commands with valid parity for the entire tXP period, while within tXP period it will
                resume parity checking and indicating parity errors on AERR. DERR remains LOW as there are no
                data bursts in progress at this time.

Self Refresh
                                   id




                Self refresh can be used to retain data in the HBM3 DRAM, even if the rest of the system is
                                 ov




                powered down. When in the self refresh mode, the HBM3 DRAM retains data without external
                clocking.
                               Pr




                SELF REFRESH ENTRY is a one-cycle command received on the row command inputs R[9:0] and
                latched with the rising and falling CK clock edges as shown in Figure 68. The command requires a
                CNOP command on the column command inputs C[7:0].

                Figure 68: SELF REFRESH ENTRY Command

                CK_c
                CK_t
                R0

                R1

                R[3:2]

                R[9:4]             V                V

                Note:      1. V = Valid (H or L)
                Self refresh entry is only allowed when all banks in both PCs are precharged with tRP satisfied, and
                when the last data elements including parity from a preceding READ command have been pushed
                out (tRDSRE). Also, all timings from other preceding commands must be satisfied (e.g. tMOD,
                t
                 RFCab, tRFCpb).
Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                          98                        ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                                Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                                     24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                                   Operation

                Once the SELF REFRESH ENTRY command is registered, R0 must be held LOW to keep the
                device in self refresh mode. For proper self refresh operation, all power supplies (VDDC, VDDQ, VDDQL,
                VPP) must be at valid levels. The HBM3 DRAM initiates a minimum of one internal refresh within
                t
                 CKSR period once it enters self refresh mode.
                To ensure that there is enough time to internally process the self refresh entry, POWER-DOWN
                ENTRY and CNOP commands have to be maintained for tCPDED period following the SELF
                REFRESH ENTRY command. Also, the CK clock must be held stable for tCKSRE cycles.
                The clocks are internally disabled during self refresh to save power. The minimum time that the
                HBM3 device must remain in self refresh mode is tCKSR. The user may halt the external clock or
                change the external clock frequency tCKSRE after self refresh entry is registered. However, the
                clock must be restarted and stable tCKSRX before the device can exit self refresh operation.




                                                                               A
