                 The procedure for exiting self refresh requires a sequence of events. First, the CK clock must be
                 stable prior to R0 going back HIGH. A delay of at least tXS must be satisfied before a valid
                 command other than MRS can be issued to the device to allow for completion of any internal
                 refresh in progress. MRS commands can be issued after tXSMRS(F) delay.
                 Parity is not evaluated for the SELF REFRESH EXIT command. The HBM3 DRAM requires RNOP
                 and CNOP commands with valid parity for the entire tXS period, while within tXSMRS period it will
                 resume parity checking and indicating parity errors on AERR. DERR remains LOW as there are no
                 data bursts in progress at this time.
                 Upon exit from self refresh, the HBM3 DRAM can be put back into self refresh mode after waiting
                 at least tXS period.

Clock Frequency Change Sequence
                 Clock frequency changes can occur during self refresh mode as described in the Self Refresh
                 section. If the change in clock frequency requires changes to configuration parameters (e.g. RL,
                 WL, PL, WR settings), MRS commands immediately prior to or after self refresh mode may be
                 required.

Temperature Compensated Refresh Reporting

Temperature Compensated Refresh Trip Points
                The HBM3 DRAM provides temperature compensated refresh related information to the controller
                via an encoding on the TEMP[1:0] outputs. The gray-coded encoding as in Table 50 defines the
                required refresh rate as determined by the hottest device in the stack to maintain data integrity. The
                reported refresh rate is updated when the junction temperature exceeds the specific trip-point
                levels appropriate for each refresh rate.

Catastrophic Temperature Sensor
                                                         un

                The CATTRIP sensor logic detects if the junction temperature of any die in the HBM3 stack
                exceeds a catastrophic trip-point level. The level is set to a value below the temperature that would
                                                ed



                result in permanent damage of the device. If the junction temperature anywhere in the stack
                exceeds that catastrophic trip-point level, the HBM3 device will drive CATTRIP to HIGH.

                The CATTRIP output is sticky in that device power-off is required to clear the CATTRIP output to
                LOW. Sufficient time should be allowed for the device to cool after a CATTRIP event. See HBM3
                Power-Up and Initialization Sequence for the initialization of the CATTRIP output.
                The circuits associated with the CATTRIP output will operate correctly even if the catastrophic trip-
                point level has been exceeded, and regardless of whether the external or internal clocks have
                stopped. The functionality of CATTRIP can be verified by writing a “1” to MR7 OP7 to force
                CATTRIP to HIGH, and “0” to set CATTRIP back to LOW.

Interconnect Redundancy Remapping
                The HBM3 DRAM supports interconnect lane remapping to help improve SIP assembly yield and
                recover functionality of the HBM3 DRAM. The SOFT_LANE_REPAIR and HARD_LANE_REPAIR
                instructions are used to perform lane remapping. Lane remapping is independent for each channel.
                The HBM3 DRAM can be programmed to retain the remapped lane information even when power
                is completely removed from the HBM3 DRAM. SOFT_LANE_REPAIR and HARD_LANE_REPAIR
                instructions can only be issued as part of the device initialization and before normal memory
                operation has commenced, e.g. before the CK clock has started to toggle.

AWORD Remapping
                There is one redundant AWORD lane per channel to either repair one lane in the row command




                                                                             A
                bus or one lane in the column command bus. APAR and ARFU are associated with the column
                command bus repair as shown in Table 53. CK_c, CK_t, and AERR signals cannot be remapped.




                                                                            D
                After a lane is remapped, the input buffer associated with the broken lane is turned off and the



                                                                    rN
                input buffer associated with the redundant bump (RA) is turned on. All functionalities are preserved
                with row or column bus lane remapping.

DWORD Remapping
                HBM3 DRAMs support remapping of one broken data bus lane per double byte. Two adjacent
                                   id




                bytes (e.g. DQ[15:0], DQ[31:16], DQ[47:32], DQ[63:48]) are treated as a pair (double byte), but
                                 ov




                each double byte is treated independently.
                After a lane is remapped, the input and output buffers associated with the broken lane are turned
                               Pr




                off and the input and output buffers associated with the redundant lane (RD) are additionally turned
                on.
                It is required to program “1111b” for the intact byte within the double byte while the remapping for
                the broken lane in the other byte is encoded according to the table.
                DBI functionality is preserved as long as the mode register setting for DBI function is enabled.
                There is no impact on the data parity function. WDQS_c, WDQS_t, RDQS_c, RDQS_t, DPAR and
                DERR signals cannot be remapped.
                During reads, the RD output drivers are enabled along with the DQ, DBI and ECC/SEV lanes of the
                physical byte the lane is located in: RD0 and RD2 are located within even bytes and thus enabled
                half a clock cycle prior to the first valid data bit, and RD1 and RD3 are located within odd bytes and
                thus enabled one clock cycle prior to the first valid data bit.

Duty Cycle Adjuster (DCA)
                HBM3 DRAMs support Duty Cycle Adjuster (DCA) that allows the memory controller to adjust the
                DRAM internally generated WDQS to compensate for a systemic duty cycle error. The DCA is
                located before the WCK divider or equivalent (see Figure 10). The DCA will affect the WDQS duty
                cycle for both Write and Read operations.
                A separate DCA is provided for each WDQS (see Table 22):
                •    the DCA for WDQS0 (PC0) is controlled via MR11 OP[3:0];
                •    the DCA for WDQS1 (PC1) is controlled via MR11 OP[7:4];
                A range of -7 steps to +7 steps is supported as shown in Figure 71 and changes the effective
                internal WDQS duty cycle as follows:




                                                                                A
                •    a positive value increases the effective tWQSH time and decreases the effective tWQSL time;




                                                                               D
                •    a negative value decreases the effective tWQSH time and increases the effective tWQSL time.


                                                                      rN
                The use of the DCA is optional for the memory controller and is not supported at CK clock
                frequencies lower than fCKDCA; at those frequencies it is required to disable the DCA by setting
                                                               de
                the DCA code to the default value (0000B).
                A duty cycle adjustment with or without a duty cycle monitor sequence shall be performed prior to
                                                        un

                WDQS-to-CK Alignment Training. The duty cycle adjustment shall be performed at the maximum
                operating frequency used by the system.
                                                ed



                An example of the effect of a DCA code change to the WDQS duty cycle is shown in Figure 72.
                The maximum offset and step size (in ps) are given in Table 61.
                                   id




                Figure 71: Duty Cycle Adjuster Range
                                 ov




                                                         Step 0 Step 3 Step 7
                               Pr




                    WDQS_t


                    WDQS_c

Duty Cycle Monitor (DCM)
                                                            un

                The HBM3 DRAM includes a duty cycle monitor (DCM) that allows the memory controller to
                observe the DRAM internal WDQS clock tree duty cycle distortion on the DERR0 output for
                                                 ed



                DWORD0 (PC0) and on the DERR1 output for DWORD 1 (PC1).
                The DCM is controlled via MR8 OP1 (see Table 19). Once DCM is enabled by setting MR8 OP1 to
                                   id




                1B, the DCM will start the WDQS duty cycle distortion measurement and provide the result on
                DERR0 and DERR1 after waiting at least tDCMM time. An even number of continuous WDQS
                                 ov




                pulses will be required for the complete duration of the measurement cycle, from the MRS
                command that initiates the measurement until the tDCMM timing has been met. The result will be
                               Pr




                available until the DCM is disabled by setting MR8 OP1 back to 0B. The DERR outputs will then
                return to their default state latest after tMOD has elapsed. The use of the DCM is not supported at
                CK clock frequencies lower than fCKDCA
                Command allowed while in this mode are REFab, REFpb, RFMab, RFMpb, RNOP, CNOP and
                MRS to disable the duty cycle monitor respectively. Internal current spikes generated by the use of
                REFab, REFpb, RFMab and RFMpb commands in this mode may negatively impact the training
                result. Controllers that cannot account for this impact should avoid use of REFab, REFpb, RFMab
                and RFMpb commands in this mode.

WDQS-to-CK Alignment Training
                WDQS-to-CK alignment training allows the host to observe the phase offset between the WDQS
                strobes in both PCs and the CK clock to aid in keeping the phase relationship within the limits given
                by the tDQSS specification. The WDQS2CK bit in MR8 OP3 is associated with this training mode.
                WDQS-to-CK alignment training is required to be performed at least once after device initialization
                if adherence to the tDQSS timing cannot be guaranteed without performing this alignment training.
                WDQS-to-CK alignment training is not required if the tDQSS timing is met. An effort to further
                narrow the WDQS-to-CK phase offset by using this training mode will not improve the stable device
                operation.
                The following steps are required for WDQS-to-CK alignment training:
Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                        110                                  ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                          Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                        24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                      Operation

                1. Enter WDQS-to-CK alignment training mode by setting the WDQS2CK bit to 1 and wait tMOD.
                   Commands allowed while in this mode are REFab, REFpb, RFMab and RFMpb, RNOP, CNOP
                   and MRS to exit WDQS-to-CK alignment training, respectively. Internal current spikes
                   generated by the use of REFab, REFpb, RFMab and RFMpb commands in this mode may
                   negatively impact the training result. Controllers that cannot account for this impact should
                   avoid use of REFab, REFpb, RFMab and RFMpb commands in this mode.
                2. Enable both WDQS0 and WDQS1 strobes; keep both strobes constantly running in order to
                   generate a valid read-out at both phase detectors with each CK clock cycle;
                3. Slowly sweep the WDQS0 and WDQS1 phases with respect to the CK clock, and monitor both
                   DERR0 and DERR1 signals for the phase detector’s result as shown in Table 63 and Figure 74;
                   each phase detector latches the 0° phase of the internally divided WDQS strobe with each
                   rising CK clock edge and provides the result on the DERR0 signal for WDQS0 and the DERR1




                                                                    A
                   signal for WDQS1 after tWDQS2PD;
                4. The ideal alignment is indicated by the phase detector output transitioning from “early” to “late”




                                                                   D
                   when the delay of the WDQS phase is continuously increased;



                                                            rN
                5. When the phase relationship between WDQS and CK meets the tDQSS specification, stop both
                   WDQS strobes; ensure that the number of WDQS pulses issued while in this training mode is
                   an even number such that the internal WDQS state is back at its reset state once the training
                                                      de
                   has finished. With that, no specific synchronization between CK and WDQS is required for
                   correct write and read operation;
                                                un

                6. Exit WDQS-to-CK alignment training mode by setting the WDQS2CK bit to 0B and wait tMOD.

WDQS Interval Oscillator
                As voltage and temperature change on the HBM3 DRAM, the WDQS clock tree delay will shift and
                may require re-training. The HBM3 DRAM includes an internal WDQS clock-tree oscillator to
                measure the amount of delay over a given time interval (determined by the controller), allowing the
                controller to compare the trained delay value to the delay value seen at a later time. The WDQS
                interval oscillator (“oscillator”) will provide the controller with important information regarding the
                need to re-train, and the magnitude of potential error. The oscillator is not associated with any
                channel and operates fully independent of any channel’s operating frequency or state (e.g. bank
                active, bank idle, power-down or self refresh). Also, no CK, WDQS or WRCK clock is required
                while the oscillator is counting. The oscillator is disabled by default upon power-up.
                The IEEE1500 instructions WOSC_RUN and WOSC_COUNT are associated with the oscillator.




                                                                      A
                Setting the WOSC_START_STOP bit in the WOSC_RUN WDR to 1 will start an internal ring
                oscillator that counts the number of times a signal propagates through a copy of the WDQS clock




                                                                     D
                tree. The oscillator is stopped by setting the WOSC_START_STOP bit back to 0. The maximum



                                                             rN
                count is 224 - 1, and the longest run time for the oscillator to not overflow the counter can be
                calculated as follows:
                Longest Run Time Interval = 224 × tRX_WDQS2DQ(min)
                                                       de
                The validity of the clock count is indicated by the WOSC_COUNT_VALID bit in the WOSC_COUNT
                                                 un

                WDR. The default state of 0 indicates an invalid count. The state is also set to 0 when the oscillator
                is started. When the oscillator stops, the WOSC_COUNT_VALID bit is set to 1B to indicate a valid
                count, and the result of the counter is stored in the WOSC_COUNT_VALUE field of the
                                          ed



                WOSC_COUNT WDR. The WOSC_COUNT_VALID bit will remain 0B (invalid) if the counter
                overflows (224 or more cycles) or if the oscillator is interrupted by pulling RESET_n to LOW. On the
                                   id




                other hand, pulling WRST_n to LOW does not impact the oscillator's operation. After the oscillator
                stops the host may issue the WOSC_COUNT instruction to read out the count.
                                 ov




                The controller may adjust the accuracy of the result by running the oscillator for shorter (less
                               Pr




                accurate) or longer (more accurate) duration. The accuracy of the result for a given temperature
                and voltage is determined by the following equation:
                                                      2 × (WDQS delay)
                WDQS Oscillator Granularity Error =
                                                          Run Time
                where:
                   •    Run Time = total time between the oscillator starting and automatically stopping;
                   •    WDQS delay = the value of the WDQS clock tree delay [tRX_WDQS2DQ(min/max)]
                Additional matching error must be included, which is the difference between WDQS training circuit
                and the actual WDQS clock tree across voltage and temperature. Therefore, the total accuracy of
                the DQS Oscillator counter is given by:
                WDQS Oscillator Accuracy = 1 - Granularity Error - Matching Error
                Example: if the total time between start and stop is 100ns, and the maximum WDQS clock tree
                delay is 400ps [tRX_WDQS2DQ(max)], then the WDQS Oscillator Granularity Error is:
                                                      2 × (0.4ns)
                WDQS Oscillator Granularity Error =                = 0.8%
                                                         100ns
                This equates to a granularity timing error of 3.2ps.
                Assuming a circuit Matching Error of 5.5ps across voltage and temperature, then the accuracy is:

tWDQS2DQ_I Offset due to Temperature and Voltage Variation
                As temperature and voltage change on the HBM3 DRAM, the WDQS clock tree will shift and may

                variation specification can be used for instances when the oscillator cannot be used to control the

Soft and Hard Repair
                The HBM3 DRAM allows to repair failing rows in the memory array using two methods:
                •    Soft repair allows a temporary row repair without using a permanent fusing mechanism. It is




                                                                       A
                     intended to enable validation that the intended repair works as expected. The IEEE1500




                                                                      D
                     SOFT_REPAIR instruction is associated with this method. A channel must be in bank idle state
                     as long as the SOFT_REPAIR instruction is loaded in the WIR.


                                                               rN
                •    Once a soft repair is validated, the user may choose to perform a fused hard repair. A Hard
                     repair is permanent and must be followed by a chip reset (RESET_n pulled LOW). The
                                                         de
                     IEEE1500 HARD_REPAIR instruction is associated with this method. All channels must be in
                     bank idle state as long as the HARD_REPAIR instruction is loaded in the WIR.
                                                   un

                Repair resources (redundant rows) are provided per PC and per bank. The number and availability
                of repair resources are provided via the HS_RES_CAP instruction. The use of soft repair will not
                                           ed



                decrement the HS_RES_CAP register so the host controller must track the resources used. If there
                is no repair resource available in a certain bank then the host controller should not issue a soft
                repair to that bank and the DRAM will ignore the programming sequence.
                                   id




                In case several soft repairs shall be performed within one PC it is required to program these soft
                                 ov




                repairs in ascending bank order.
                               Pr




                The repair granularity indicating the number of repaired rows per a single soft or hard repair is
                sixteen rows. The row address bits associated with each repair are indicated in the PPR_RA field
                of the DEVICE_ID WDR and listed in Table 65.

                Table 65: Associated Row Addresses
                                                       Associated Row Addresses
                               RA12                   RA2                       RA1                               RA0

                The soft repair supports an Undo and Lock function. The soft repair Undo will restore a previously
                used repair resource back to its unused state and at the same time reactivate the original
                (unrepaired) row instead. A locked repair resource cannot be set back to the unused state using
                the Undo function.
                For this HBM3 DRAM the availability of the Undo and Lock functions and the number of available
                repair resources for soft repair are configurable via the SPPRUL bit in MR10 OP0.
                •    with the bit set to 0B (default), four repair resource are available per PC and per bank; in this
                     case the Undo and Lock feature is not supported and the corresponding bits in the
                     SOFT_REPAIR WDR are ignored.
                •    with the bit set to 1B, one repair resource is available per PC and per bank; in this case the
                     Undo and Lock feature is supported.

Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                116                             ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                             Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                           24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                         Operation

                The selection shall be made during device initialization: once Soft Repair Undo / Lock has been
                enabled, it must remain enabled; disabling the feature must be followed by a chip reset (RESET_n
                = LOW).
                The host controller can lock down a used soft repair resource by issuing a soft repair with the
                SOFT_REPAIR_LOCK and SOFT_REPAIR_START bits as 1B. A locked repair resource cannot be
                set back to the unused state using the Undo function. Only a chip reset (RESET_n pulled LOW) or
                power-cycling can unlock a locked repair resource
                The Undo and Lock functions are mutually exclusive and therefore must not be set 1B at the same
                time when issuing a soft repair.
                When using soft repair specifically with the Undo function, the host controller must manage and
                schedule the refresh operation properly on the valid data of a row address. If a row has been




                                                                       A
                repaired, all refresh commands will exclude the original row from being refreshed and refresh the




                                                                      D
                repair row instead. Similarly, unused repair resources will not be refreshed which includes those
                resources that had been allocated but were then set back to the unused state using the Undo


                                                                   rN
                operation. Especially when switching back and forth between an original and a repair row, regular
                refresh commands may not hit both rows within the required refresh interval. A possible method to
                                                         de
                prevent a potential data loss is to explicitly issue ACTIVATE and PRECHARGE commands to the
                mapped-out rows before and after the soft repair operations.
                                                   un

Self Repair
                The HBM3 DRAM supports self repair to help improve SIP assembly yield or to achieve a high
                                             ed



                level of system reliability by scanning for and repairing failures in the HBM3 during the initialization
                process.
                                   id




                IEEE1500 instructions SELF_REP and SELF_REP_RESULTS are associated with the self repair
                                 ov




                functionality. Self repair is initiated by loading the SELF_REP instruction. Since the instruction
                works on 8 channels at a time, WIR [12:8] must be set to either 1CH or 1DH to select one half of the
                               Pr




                16 channels to run on. A parallel operation of Self Repair on both groups of 8 channels is not
                supported. See Table 75 for the mapping of channels for 1CH and 1DH.
                The clock sources for SELF_REP is the WRCK clock which must be constantly running while the
                SELF_REP instruction is loaded in the WIR.
                Figure 77 provides a flow chart showing the 3 flows for the REP_TYPE field (bits[3:2]) of the
                SELF_REP instruction. Setting REP_TYPE to 11B will instruct the HBM3 DRAM to start the first
                phase of the self repair process which is self-test to identify any hard failures. The SELF_REP
                instruction works on one SID at a time and must be run on each SID separately by using the
                SID_SELECT field (bits [5:4]). The number of SELF_REP instructions required to check all
                channels and SIDs is listed in Table 66. The SELFR_REF_RATE field (bits [7:6]) must be set by
                the host to control temperature compensated refresh rate.

                Table 66: SELF_REP Instructions vs. Stack Height
                            Stack Height          SID_SELECT          Minimum Number of SELF_REP Instructions
                                   8-High            00B, 01B                               4
                                   12-High         00B, 01B, 10B                            6

                The self-test will use vendor specific pattern(s) that detect hard failures in the HBM3 DRAM. Once
                the self-test phase is complete the HBM3 DRAM will proceed to the auto-repair phase. The auto-

Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                  117                          ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                                  Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                                            24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                                          Operation

                repair automatically repairs up to 8 failed addresses (up to 2 per memory slice, see Table 4) from
                the self-test phase.
                SELF_REP may be issued any time after the device has been properly initialized, specifically after
                t
                 INIT3 has been met, and the HBM3 DRAM is in the all banks idle state.
                This HBM3 DRAM shares repair resources between soft repair, hard repair and self repair as
                indicated by the SHARED_REP_RES field of the DEVICE_ID WDR being set to 1B. If the DRAM
                shares the resources the host can use the HS_REP_CAP instruction to tell how many resources
                are available in each channel for self repair. Any repair done by self repair will update the
                resources per bank in that channel.
                Because of the shared resources, the DRAM must not use all the available resources in a bank.
                One resource per bank must be left for the host to perform soft repair. If the host desires to allow




                                                                                    A
                self repair to use all of the shared resources then the SHARED_OVERRIDE field can be set to 1B.




                                                                                   D
                Before any self repair, the host is recommended to clear any soft repairs using the “undo” function



                                                                        rN
                on the channels the host plans to run self repair, or a chip reset. Failure to do so could result in the
                DRAM using the shared resources and operation is then not guaranteed. After the self repair is
                complete the host can perform soft repair(s) after checking if resources are available.
                                                                 de
                Table 67 illustrates the expected behavior of the HBM3 DRAM and the expected

                              set to 0B. In that case no repair is performed.
                           2. This HBM3 DRAM performs up to 8 repairs per SELF_REP (up to 2 repairs per memory slice).
                           3. After the initial SELF_REP the DRAM will report 'fails remain'; the host will need to issue a second
                              SELF_REP to repair the other fail. After that the results will be 'no fails remain'.
                           4. The host has the option to do no further repair and leave the remaining resource for soft repair, or use up the
                              one remaining resource with an additional SELF_REP.

                During the self repair process the host can poll the DRAM for the status using the SR_PROGRESS
                field of the SELF_REP instruction. The DRAM will report whether the self-test is in progress (01B),
                the auto-repair is in progress (10B) or the self repair process has completed (11B) or is not running
                (00B). This reporting is the same for all 8 channels in the channel group selected by WIR[12:8]. The
                SELF_REP instruction must be kept in the WIR during this time.


Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                         118                                        ©2025 Micron Technology, Inc. All rights reserved.
                                           Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                           24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM

                Once the self repair process is complete, the SELF_REP_RESULTS instruction can be issued to
                read out the results. The DRAM will report the results for each SID and will indicate whether fails
                remain (01B), whether unrepairable fails remain (10B), whether SELF_REP should be run again
                (11B), or whether self repair has not run since the initialization or no fails remain after most recent
                run (00B).
                If after running both the self-test and auto-repair phases the results indicate that fails remain, the
                SELF_REP instruction can be issued to run only the auto-repair phase to repair additional fails by
                setting the REP_TYPE to 10B. With REP_TYPE set to 10B the DRAM will repair one additional row
                address from the previous self-test phase. If additional fails remain, the host can continue to issue
                SELF_REP instructions with REP_TYPE = 10B, followed by SELF_REP_RESULTS, until the
                DRAM reports 00B to indicate that there are no fails remaining. If the DRAM reports 11B, this is an
                indication to the host to run SELF_REP again with either REP_TYPE set to 01B (self-test only) or




                                                                       A
                11B (self-test and auto-repair) to load internal fail addresses from the self-test phase.




                                                                      D
                With REP_TYPE set to 01B, the SELF_REPAIR instruction will only run the self-test phase and the



                                                              rN
                host can check the results after completion to decide on next steps.
                If the host runs the auto-repair only without previously having run the self test phase, then the
                                                        de
                SELF_REP_RESULTS instruction will report 00B as there are no failing address(es).
                If the DRAM reports that unrepairable fails remain (10B) on a channel, this indicates that there are
                                                  un

                not enough repair elements remaining to repair fail addresses latched during the self-test phase.
                The host can decide whether to run self repair again to repair other channels or complete the repair
                process.
                                          ed



                Once the self repair process is complete, the host must issue a reset by driving RESET_n to LOW
                and then following the Initialization Sequence with Stable Power.

                                 ov

                               Pr

Loopback Test Modes
                    A Multiple-Input Shift Register (MISR) / Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) circuit is defined
                    within the HBM3 AWORD and DWORD I/O blocks. These circuits are intended for testing and
                    training the link between the host and the HBM3 DRAM.
                    Referring to Figure 78, each byte within a DWORD implements a 40-bit MISR/LFSR circuit
                    comprised of 4 QDR bits (Q0 to Q3) for each of the 10 data signals (8 DQ, DBI and ECC/SEV).
                    These 4 QDR bits represent the 4 UI per CK clock cycle latched by WDQS on writes or driven
                    along with RDQS on reads. Note that a BL8 write or read burst is 2 tCK long and thus corresponds
                    to two steps of the DWORD MISR/LFSR. The MISR/ LFSR circuits operate independently across
                    the bytes.
                    The AWORD implements a 38-bit MISR/LFSR circuit comprised of two DDR bits (Rise/ Fall) for




                                                                                          A
                    each of the 18 row and column command/address inputs including ARFU.




                                                                                         D
                    When the MISR content is read via the IEEE 1500 port DWORD_MISR instruction, the four bytes



                                                                               rN
                    per DWORD (160 bits) for the two DWORDs within a channel are serially shifted out, providing a
                    total of 320 bits. The 38-bit AWORD MISR content is read via the AWORD_MISR instruction. See
                    Table 86 and Table 87, respectively, for the bit-order for both registers.
                                                                          de
                    The term MISR modes collectively refers to all of the modes - LFSR mode, register mode, MISR
                    mode, and LFSR compare mode. AWORD MISR modes and DWORD MISR modes refer to all of
                                                                 un

                    the modes defined for the specific bus.

                Figure 79 shows an example of a 4-bit Galois type MISR/LFSR structure that implements the

                f(x) = X4 + X3 + 1

                implement a preset function, where specific bits are set to logic 1.

AWORD MISR Polynomial
                The AWORD MISR structure is a 38-bit MISR/LFSR with the following polynomial:
                   f(x) = X38 + X6 + X5 + X + 1
                The AWORD MISR may be serially accessed via the AWORD_MISR instruction.

DWORD MISR Polynomial
                The DWORD MISR structure is a 40-bit MISR/LFSR per byte with the following polynomial:
                f(x) = X40 + X38 + X21 + X19 + 1
                The DWORD MISRs are accessed via the DWORD_MISR instruction. The 4 bytes per DWORD
                and the two DWORDs per channels are concatenated into a 320-bit WDR.

General Loopback Modes Features and Behavior
                This section addresses features and behaviors that generally apply to all of the MISR modes.
                a) Entering the MISR modes: MISR modes may be enabled after tINIT3 within the initialization
                   sequence; they may also be entered any time after completing the initialization (see
                   Initialization). DWORD MISR modes are controlled via Mode Register 7 (MR7), while AWORD
                   MISR modes are controlled via the IEEE1500 port AWORD_MISR_CONFIG instruction.
                   AWORD and DWORD MISR modes cannot be used simultaneously since the DWORD MISR
                   modes are driven via READ and WRITE commands on the AWORD bus.
                b) Entering and exiting AWORD MISR modes: HBM3 DRAMs allow the AWORD MISR modes
                   to be utilized on one or more channels while the other channels continue to operate normally.
                   After normal initialization, to enter the AWORD MISR modes the host must put the desired




                                                                     A
                   channel(s) into either precharge power-down or self refresh mode. Self refresh mode may be




                                                                    D
                   used in order to retain memory content while using the AWORD MISR modes, as needed.
                   Enabling the AWORD MISR modes re-enables the AWORD input buffers that are normally


                                                             rN
                   disabled in power-down and self refresh modes, which may result in increased current draw
                   over the IDD2P, IDD2P0 and IDD6x specifications. If returning to normal operation is not
                                                       de
                   required, the host may assert an initialization sequence per section Initialization after operating
                   the AWORD MISR modes. The sequence for entering AWORD MISR modes, and then exiting
                   back to normal operation is as follows:
                                                 un

                1) At any time after initializing the HBM3 DRAM enters the all banks idle state.
                2) Enter either the precharge power-down or self refresh. Maintain R0 = LOW while in these
                                         ed



                   modes.
                                   id




                3) Stop the CK clock with CK_t = LOW and CK_c = HIGH.
                                 ov




                4) Enable/enter and operate the AWORD MISR modes (AWORD_MISR_CONFIG ENABLE = 1B).
                   Finish these operations with CK stopped (CK_t = LOW, CK_c = HIGH) and R0 = LOW.
                               Pr




                5) Disable the AWORD MISR modes and follow the power-down or self refresh exit procedures.
                6) When using the AWORD MISR modes after tINIT3 within the initialization sequence, power-
                   down or self refresh entry and exit does not apply.
                     If the DRAM is not required to continue with mission mode operation after AWORD MISR test,
                     there is no requirement on the row/column command bus and the precharge power-down or
                     self refresh state after loopback test. The AWORD_MISR_ CONFIG enable bit can be reset by
                     WRST_n during a subsequent initialization sequence.
                c) Entering and exiting DWORD MISR modes: HBM3 DRAMs allow the DWORD MISR modes
                   to be utilized on one or more channels while the other channels continue to operate normally.
                   After normal initialization, to enter the DWORD MISR modes the host must put the desired
                   channel(s) into the all banks idle state, enable the DWORD MISR modes (MR7 OP0 = 1B; see
                   Table 17), and then enter precharge power-down or self refresh mode. Self refresh mode may
                   be used in order to retain memory content while using the DWORD MISR modes, as needed.
                   Enabling the DWORD MISR modes before entering precharge power-down or self refresh
                   keeps the AWORD and DWORD I/O buffers enabled and may result in increased current draw
                   over the IDD2P, IDD2P0 and IDD6x specifications. DWORD MISR modes may also be enabled
                   after tINIT3 within the initialization sequence. Also see items h), k), and n) for related DWORD
                   MISR modes configuration setting. On the column command bus only READ (RD), WRITE
                   (WR), and CNOP commands may be issued which operate the DWORD MISR modes, MR7
                   MRS commands to select the DWORD MISR modes, and MR15 MRS command to adjust the

                                 ov




                   is not active when loopback test mode is enabled and the RPAR setting in MR0 has no effect.
                   To generate traffic on the DPAR signal a nearby DQ signal is copied on the DPAR signal: DQ2
                               Pr




                   is sent on DPAR0 (DWORD0), and DQ34 is sent on DPAR1 (DWORD1), irrespective of any

                   DRAM’s parity evaluation logic is active when loopback test mode is enabled and outputs
                   results on AERR after tPARAC and on DERR after tPARDQ, respectively, if the parity
                   calculation is enabled in MR0 (see Table 10). The parity latency in MR1 (see Table 11) must be
                   set to a supported PL value. The HBM3 DRAM will process write parity per the PL setting and
                   protocol, including any required additional WDQS cycles. A suggested host-side
                   implementation is to use signature register circuits for checking the correctness of the AERR
                   and DERR signals. It is also suggested that the host generate data on the DWORD DPAR
                   signals in order to exercise these signal paths and logic.
                i)   Preset state AAAAAAAAAAh and 2AAAAAAAAAh: the preset state for the DWORD MISR is
                     AAAAAAAAAAh. This is a useful state for producing an alternating 0-1 pattern on all 10 bits
                     associated with a DWORD byte when put into Register mode (read direction). This basic
                     pattern may be used by the host for RDQS eye centering. READ commands from the DWORD
                     MISR are supported in Preset state. WRITE and READ commands to and from the DWORD
                     MISR do not change the DWORD MISR content in this mode.

                                   id




                   expected to stop CK toggling, enable the desired AWORD MISR mode, and then start sending
                   CK toggles and AWORD data. To avoid timing impairment on the CK startup cycle, the HBM3
                                 ov




                   DRAM will treat the first received CK cycle as a preamble clock cycle and not process the data
                   on the AWORD signals in MISR or register mode, nor compare them in LFSR compare mode.
                               Pr




                   The MISR block will keep its state unchanged during this filter cycle. The first clock cycle filter
                   circuit is enabled by setting AWORD_MISR_CONFIG bits [1:0] = 00B. The first data sampled by
                   the HBM3 DRAM is on the second CK clock cycle. Only the very first CK clock cycle will be
                   filtered. If the host were to stop and restart CK clocking while remaining in an AWORD MISR
                   mode without applying another preset, the AWORD data will be sampled on the starting clock
                   cycle, with possible CK edge timing impairment.

AWORD and DWORD MISR Modes (Write direction)
                When the AWORD or DWORD MISR modes are active, the data on the AWORD or DWORD data
                signals is received based on the CK clock or WDQS strobes respectively and compressed in the
                MISRs. The host is in complete control of the number of data cycles that are sent, and if
                successfully received by the HBM3 DRAM the values captured in the respective MISRs will be
                repeatable and deterministic.

AWORD and DWORD Register Modes (Write direction)
                When the AWORD or DWORD register modes are active, the data on the AWORD or DWORD
                data signals is received based on the CK clock or WDQS strobes respectively and stored directly
                into the respective MISR without compression. Effectively the AWORD MISR operates as a 2-bit
                storage register and will store the AWORD data of the last CK cycle, and the DWORD MISR
                operate will store the last 4 UI of the last write burst.

DWORD Register Mode (Read direction)
                The content of DWORD MISRs may be read via the data bus. The DWORD read mux control bit in
                MR7 selects either the MISR or the LFSR Compare sticky error bits as data source. Issue READ
                commands and the HBM3 DRAM will produce RDQS preamble and postamble strobes and send
                DWORD data consistent with the read protocols.
                Intended uses for the various read data sources include the following:
                a) Reading the sticky error bits after an LFSR Compare mode test sequence by setting MR7 OP1
                   = 1B. Sticky error data is a single data bit per signal and is output as static values on the
                   interface for a full read burst.
                b) Reading a basic clock pattern on all or select signals for DWORD read link training from MISR
                   by setting MR7 OP1 = 0B; with the data pattern being set before using the DWORD MISR

AWORD and DWORD LFSR Compare Modes (Write direction)
                The LFSR compare modes enable direct identification of failing signal connections between the
                host and HBM. It is assumed that the host implements LFSR data generators that match the
Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                        130
                                              Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                           24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                         Operation

                lengths and polynomials of the HBM3 DRAM’s LFSRs, and that the host and HBM3 DRAM LFSRs
                start and run in synch. The LFSRs generate data on each signal, and the compare circuitry check
                for matching data for each data unit interval (UI). Any mismatch between the data received and the
                data predicted by the LFSR will set the sticky error bit for the respective signal(s). The first data
                cycle expected from the host and compared by the HBM3 DRAM will be the LFSR’s initial state,
                based on preset or an alternate seed value if loaded.
                Once a miscompare is found on a signal, its sticky error bit is set to 1B for the remainder of the test.
                The sticky error bits may be read via the READ_LFSR_COMPARE_STICKY instruction. DWORD
                related sticky error bits may also be read via the data bus while AWORD sticky error bits can only
                be read via the IEEE1500 test port. The sticky error bits are reset to 0B via the MR7 OP[5:3] = 000B
                for the DWORD related bits, and AWORD_MISR_CONFIG MODE[1:0] = 00B.

                                                                                         Direct Access (DA) Test Port


Direct Access (DA) Test Port
                A direct access (DA) test port is available via DA[39:0] for vendor specific test implementations.
                Two microbumps are associated with each DA signal. A depopulated area for probing is located
                close to the DA port region in columns 21 to 36 of the HBM3 bump matrix (see Microbump Matrix).
                Access to the DA test port is controlled via signal DA0. When DA0 = LOW, DA[39:1] drivers are in
                Hi-Z and input receivers are disabled allowing the bus to float. When DA0 = HIGH, DA[39:1] are
                enabled for vendor specific test features and the IEEE 1500 port is disabled. CATTRIP and
                TEMP[1:0] outputs remain active, but their state may not be valid and shall be ignored. The DA0
                input is equipped with an internal pull-down resistor which ensures that DA0 is held LOW and the
                test port remains inactive even if DA0 is left floating.
                If the DA test port is not used in the system, it is recommended to tie all DA port signals to VSS.




                                                                            A
                The DA test port may be enabled at any time after the power ramp has been completed and all




                                                                           D
                supply voltages are within their defined ranges (tINIT0), and after waiting for at least tINIT1 time.



                                                                 rN
                The level of the RESET_n input shall be irrelevant for DA test port enabling.
                The DA test port may be disabled at any time by pulling DA0 to LOW. The HBM3 DRAM may then
                                                           de
                resume normal operation by after performing a chip reset followed by a device initialization as
                described in the Initialization Sequence with Stable Power section.
                                                     un

                18 DA signals are designated to connect point-to-point to each HBM3 DRAM. 22 signals are
                designated to connect in parallel to up to four HBM3 DRAM devices on a multi drop bus as shown
                in Figure 84. The function of each of these signals is vendor specific. Table 72 defines which DA
                                               ed



                signals are allocated for point-to-point and for multi drop.

DA Test Port Lockout
                The DA test port can be disabled (locked) by setting MR8 OP0 bit to 1B. The bit is defined for
                channels a or e only. Once the bit is set to 1B, the DA test port will remain disabled unless power is
                removed from the HBM3 DRAM. Any chip reset through pulling RESET_n LOW or via IEEE1500
                HBM_RESET instruction or writing a 0B via an MRS command or IEEE1500 instruction
                MODE_REGISTER_DUMP_SET will not clear the locked state.

                                                                                                                    IEEE1500 Test Port


IEEE1500 Test Port
                 The IEEE Standard 1500 compliant test access port provides a direct test connection between a
                 host and the HBM3 DRAM. The HBM3 DRAM’s test port extends the standard specification and
                 replicates the WSO output per channel. This allows some instructions to be executed in parallel
                 across channels and eliminates the need for cross-channel arbitration for WSO.
                 IEEE1500 operations may be asserted at any time after device initialization and during normal
                 memory operation including when the HBM3 DRAM is in power-down or self refresh mode. See
                 section Interaction with Mission Mode Operation for how the various instructions interact with
                 normal operation, and requirements for returning to normal operation. See also section Initialization
                 Sequence For Use Of IEEE1500 Instructions Including Lane Repair for a subset of operations that
                 are allowed before the device initialization has been completed.




                                                                                  A
                 Please refer to ieee.org for more details about the IEEE1500 standard.




                                                                                 D

                 possible to operate the HBM3 DRAM without using the test ports. In this case both DA0 and
                                                                 de
                 WRST_n must be pulled LOW to prevent the device from entering test modes.
                 Table 73 summarizes the status of the test access port signals.

                 Figure 85 shows the HBM3 DRAM’s IEEE1500 compliant architecture that uses an asymmetrical
                 WSP (Wrapper Serial Port) with a single WSI and sixteen per channel WSOs. The standard
                                                 ed



                 compliant register stack is shown in the figure, including the Wrapper Bypass Register (WBY),
                 Wrapper Boundary Register (WBR), and Wrapper Data Registers (WDR). The C, S and U notation
                 for the registers refer to Capture, Shift and Update respectively, and indicate for each of the
                                     id




                 registers which functions are supported by that register. For example, the WBY only provides a
                                   ov




                 Shift stage, whereas the WDRs provide Shift/ Capture and Update stages.
                 The WSO[a:p] output drivers are permanently enabled with their drive state being LOW, HIGH, or
                                 Pr




                 undefined based on the current instruction loaded into the WIR. For example, if BYPASS is the
                 current instruction, then WSO output data is defined only after one or more WRCK clock cycles
                 have been applied. A WSO output will drive a LOW when a channel is disabled via the
                 CHANNEL_DISABLE instruction or marked as “not present / not working” in the DEVICE_ID WDR.
                 The Wrapper Instruction Register (WIR) logic is included in Figure 85, and Figure 86 shows further
                 details of the WIR implementation. The WIR is described in the IEEE1500 Test Access Port
                 Instruction Register section, and the instructions supported by this HBM3 DRAM in the Test
                 Instructions section.
                 The five channel select bits of the WIR shift stage in Figure 86 are decoded to generate the
                 CHSelect[a:p] outputs which control the per channel operation of the instructions. When a channel
                 is not selected for an active instruction, then the CAPTUREWDR[a:p], SHIFTWDR[a:p] and
                 UPDATEWDR[a:p] enables of the WSP are gated off. This will disable the WDRs of unselected
                 channels for the decoded instruction. This gating is shown by the logic AND gates at the output of
                 the de-multiplexer in Figure 85.

Test Access Port Wrapper Data Register (WDR) Types

Read-Only WDRs
                 WDR bit fields that are specified as read-only capture data into the shift stage register when a
                 CaptureWR event is performed. The read-only WDRs keep their state during an UpdateWR event
                 and do not have an update stage register. Read-only WDRs shift out their content during a ShiftWR
                 event. Data shifted into WSI during the ShiftWR event is ignored.

Write-Only WDRs
                 WDR bit fields that are specified as write-only copy all data bits into the update stage register when
                 an UpdateWR event is performed. When a write-only WDR is connected between WSI and WSO,
                 any CaptureWR event has no effect on the WDR. Write-only WDRs shift out their content during
                 the ShiftWR event.

Read and Write WDRs
                 Read/Write WDRs operate as merged function of write-only and read-only WDRs. They capture
                 data bits into the shift stage register during a CaptureWR event and copy bits from the shift stage
                 into the update stage simultaneously when the UpdateWR event is performed.

WDR Bit Order
                The LSB (bit 0) of each WDR is located nearest to the serial output (WSO) and shifted out first.
                WSO output timing and valid data window are defined in Table 104.

WDR Reset State
                Asserting WRST_n to LOW asynchronously asserts these states on the HBM3 DRAM’s IEEE1500
                test port logic:
                •     all WDRs place their update and / or shift stages (where applicable) into a state that ensures
                      that the HBM3 DRAM returns to mission mode operation and all test modes are disabled;
                •     the WIR is set to BYPASS, effectively clearing any prior EXTEST_RX, EXTEST_TX, or
                      CHANNEL_ID instruction, thus returning all functional signals to their normal functional mode.




                                                                        A
                      Boundary scan chain content is undefined;




                                                                       D
                •     No change to any previously loaded SOFT_REPAIR, HARD_REPAIR, SOFT_LANE_REPAIR,


                                                                rN
                      or HARD_LANE_REPAIR register content;
                •     the content of the DWORD_MISR and AWORD_MISR is undefined;
                                                        de
                •     the AWORD MISR is disabled by setting bit 2 in the AWORD_MISR_CONFIG WDR to 0;
                                                    un

                •     the CHANNEL_DISABLE WDR is reset (refer to the CHANNEL_DISABLE instruction for
                      conditions to re-enable a disabled channel);
                •

BYPASS
                                 ov




                 The BYPASS instruction places a single bit WDR between WSI and each channel’s WSO. Data is
                 shifted from WSI to WSO through the one-bit WDR by WRCK.
                               Pr




                 BYPASS is the default instruction after asserting WRST_n to LOW.
                 Wrapper Data Register: when BYPASS is the current instruction, the 1-bit shift register as shown
                 in Table 77 is connected between WSI and WSO[a:p], and the WSO outputs of all active channels
                 drive the same data during ShiftWR events.
                 CaptureWR: when BYPASS is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will have no effect.
                 UpdateWR: when BYPASS is the current instruction, the UpdateWR event will have no effect.

EXTEST_RX and EXTEST_TX
                EXTEST_RX and EXTEST_TX are both intended for DC I/O connectivity testing similar to board
                level boundary scan. The receive notation in EXTEST_RX designates that the HBM3 I/O will
                sample the logic value and capture into the data register the value that is present at the micro
                bump interface. The transmit notation in EXTEST_TX designates that the HBM3 I/O will drive the
                logic value shifted into the data register at the micro bump interface. All HBM3 bidirectional I/O,
                inputs and outputs support both instructions. Differential inputs and outputs (CK_t/CK_c,
                WDQS_t/WDQS_c and RDQS_t/RDQS_c) also support both instructions on both the true and
                complement signals. Note that CK_t/CK_c, WDQS_t/WDQS_c, and RDQS_t/RDQS_c require a
                differential input signal (L/H or H/L) in EXTEST_RX.
                While EXTEST_RX is the current instruction, all functional signals of the selected channel(s) enter




                                                                                A
                a High-Z state, including the output-only signals AERR, DERR, RDQS_t/RDQS_c, TEMP[1:0] and
                CATTRIP. See also the Boundary Scan section.




                                                                               D
                I/O signals power up in input mode by default. The host will put all AWORD and DWORD drivers


                                                                       rN
                into High-Z state prior to loading the EXTEST_TX instruction into the WIR. As soon as
                EXTEST_TX becomes the current instruction, all AWORD and DWORD signals will change to
                                                                de
                output mode and remain in output mode until reset of the test logic or until a different instruction is
                updated on the channel.
                                                           un

                A channel disabled either via the corresponding CHANNEL_AVAILABLE bit in the DEVICE ID
                WDR or via the CHANNEL_DISABLE instruction will not respond to the EXTEST_TX or
                EXTEST_RX instructions.
                                                     ed



                Wrapper Data Register: when EXTEST_RX or EXTEST_TX is the current instruction, the
                Wrapper Boundary Register (WBR) as shown in Table 78 is connected between WSI and WSO.
                                   id




                CaptureWR: when EXTEST_RX is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will capture the
                                 ov




                input values into the shift stage of the WBR. The captured data is shifted out on WSO during a
                subsequent ShiftWR event. Inputs must be stable for the setup and hold times tSEXT and tHEXT.
                               Pr




                When EXTEST_TX is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will have no effect.
                ShiftWR: the Wrapper Boundary Register (WBR) does not provide an update stage. When
                EXTEST_TX is the current instruction, the value driven on the outputs is directly derived from the
                WBR’s shift stage and will update with each ShiftWR event. The new data will be stable after
                t
                 OVEXT time.
                UpdateWR: when EXTEST_RX or EXTEST_TX is the current instruction, the UpdateWR event will
                have no effect.

                Table 78: Wrapper Boundary Register (WBR)
                     Bits                    Field           Type                            Description
                                                                    Signals in MIDSTACK region
                     121           RESET_n                      I - channel b only
                                   TEMP0                      I/O - channel n only (see note 1)
                                   0                            I - channels a, c to m, o and p (reserved bit)
                                                                    Signals in MIDSTACK region
                     120           TEMP1                      I/O - channel n only (see note 1)
                                   CATTRIP                    I/O - channel o only (see note 1)
                                   0                            I   channels a to m and p (reserved bit)

HBM_RESET
                                   id




                The HBM_RESET instruction initiates an asynchronous functional reset of the HBM3 DRAM,
                                 ov




                equivalent to asserting RESET_n to LOW.
                The HBM_RESET condition is not self-clearing. Instead, the reset state must explicitly be set and
                               Pr




                cleared. To accomplish an HBM3 reset, the HBM_RESET bit must be held as 1B for a minimum
                duration of tRES which equals tPW_RESET (see Initialization Sequence with Stable Power
                Sequence with Stable Power).
                It is pointed out that the Wrapper Serial Port (WSP) itself including the associated control logic and
                WDRs is not reset by the HBM_RESET instruction. The DA port signals are also not affected by
                the HBM_RESET instruction.
                Wrapper Data Register: when HBM_RESET is the current instruction, the data register as shown
                in Table 79 is connected between WSI and WSO[a:p], and the WSO outputs of all active channels
                drive the same data during ShiftWR events.
                CaptureWR: when HBM_RESET is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will have no
                effect.
                UpdateWR: when HBM_RESET is the current instruction, the UpdateWR event will load the value
                from the shift stage into the update stage and initiate or clear the functional reset.

                Table 79: HBM_RESET Wrapper Data Register
                     Bits                   Field            Type                               Description
                        0          HBM_RESET                   W     0B - Clear the functional reset
                                                                     1B - Initiate the functional reset

Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                          145
                                             Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                              24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                      IEEE1500 Test Port

                Internally, the RESET_n signal and the HBM_RESET instruction are logically combined such that
                when either is true then the internal reset state is true. During power-up it is required that WRST_n
                be driven LOW, thus ensuring that the uninitialized IEEE1500 test port logic does not interfere with
                the power-up initialization sequence.

                Figure 88: RESET_n and HBM_RESET Logic

                  HBM_RESET
                  (active HIGH)
                                                                           Internal reset
                  RESET_n
                                                                           state
                  (active LOW)
                After the power-up initialization, the RESET_n input is HIGH, and subsequent stable power resets




                                                                        A
                may be asserted by either driving the RESET_n input LOW, or by using the HBM_RESET




                                                                       D
                instruction. Note that the HBM_RESET instruction does not bring the HBM3 DRAM out of reset



                                                               rN
                while the external RESET_n input is driven LOW. Similarly, the HBM3 DRAM cannot be brought
                out of reset using the RESET_n input while reset is asserted using the HBM_RESET instruction.

MBIST
                The MBIST instruction controls the device hosted memory built in self-test along with the
                               Pr




                MBIST_SUMMARY and MBIST_REPAIR_VECTOR instructions.
                Either a stable CK clock on channels g and h (CKg_t/_c, CKh_t/c), or a stable WRCK clock are
                required as reference clock source while MBIST is active.
                Wrapper Data Register: when MBIST is the current instruction, the data register as shown in
                Table 81 will be connected between WSI and WSO.
                CaptureWR: when MBIST is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will capture the read bit
                fields into the shift stage of the WDR.
                UpdateWR: when MBIST is the current instruction, the UpdateWR event will simultaneously load
                all write bit fields from the shift stage to the update stage of the WDR.

SOFT_REPAIR
                The SOFT_REPAIR instruction allows a temporary row repair without using a permanent fusing
                                                   ed



                mechanism. It is intended to enable validation that the intended repair works as expected. If power
                is removed from the device or a chip reset occurs with RESET_n pulled LOW, the soft repair will
                                   id




                revert to the un-repaired state.
                                 ov




                A channel must be in all bank idle state as long as the SOFT_REPAIR instruction is loaded in the
                WIR.
                               Pr




                Wrapper Data Register: when SOFT_REPAIR is the current instruction, the data register as
                shown in Table 84 will be connected between WSI and WSO.
                CaptureWR: when SOFT_REPAIR is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will have no
                effect.
                UpdateWR: when SOFT_REPAIR is the current instruction, the UpdateWR event will simulta-
                neously load all bit fields from the shift stage into the update stage. Completion of the update event
                will initiate the soft repair sequence which will be completed after tSREP time. A stable WRCK
                clock is required during tSREP time.

CHANNEL_ID
                                 ov




                This instruction enables the HBM channel identification by driving all bidirectional DWORD I/Os to
                               Pr




                HIGH unless a channel is disabled either via the corresponding CHANNEL_AVAILABLE bit in the
                DEVICE ID WDR or via the CHANNEL_DISABLE instruction. In these cases a channel will not
                respond to the CHANNEL_ID instruction.
                Wrapper Data Register: when CHANNEL_ID is the current instruction, the data register as shown
                in Table 88 is connected between WSI and WSO.
                CaptureWR: when CHANNEL_ID is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will have no
                effect.
                UpdateWR: when CHANNEL_ID is the current instruction, the UpdateWR event will load the
                enable bit from the shift stage into the update stage of the WDR. All bidirectional DWORD I/Os
                (DQ, DBI, RD, ECC/SEV and DPAR) will drive a HIGH latest after tOVCHN when the enable bit is
                1B, and return to their default state latest after tOZCHN when the enable bit is 0B or a different
                instruction has been loaded in the WIR. Output pins RDQS_t/_c and DERR maintain their default
                states regardless of the CHANNEL_ID instruction. DBI, ECC/SEV and DPAR will drive a HIGH
                even if the respective function is disabled in the mode register.

                                                                   1B –TX drive a HIGH

                This instruction is used to capture the LFSR Compare Sticky error data to be shifted out on the
                WSO output. The instruction is associated with the AWORD and DWORD I/O loopback test
                features. Data register bit positions are specified in Table 93. Note that the content of the MISR

                MISR_CONFIG preset) before continuing with additional testing. See Loopback Test Modes for
                MISR mode features and usage.

                While both the AWORD and DWORD sticky error bits share a common WDR, the bits are set and
                cleared only by their respective AWORD or DWORD Preset and LFSR Compare operations. For
                example, an AWORD_MISR_CONFIG preset operation clears the AWORD sticky error bits, and
                the state of the DWORD sticky error bits is undefined; therefore, the host should ignore the
                DWORD sticky error bits when operating the AWORD LFSR Compare mode. Conversely, the
                DWORD_MISR_CONFIG preset operation clears the DWORD sticky error bits, and the state of the
                AWORD sticky error bits is undefined; therefore, the host should ignore the AWORD sticky error
                bits when operating the DWORD LFSR Compare mode.

SOFT_LANE_REPAIR and HARD_LANE_REPAIR
                The SOFT_LANE_REPAIR and HARD_LANE_REPAIR instructions convey lane remapping and
                                                 ed



                repair information. Both instructions share the same LANE_REPAIR WDR. SOFT_LANE_REPAIR
                and HARD_LANE_REPAIR instructions can only be issued as part of the device initialization and
                                   id




                before normal memory operation has commenced, e.g. before the CK clock has started to toggle.
                                 ov




                Wrapper Data Register: the LANE_REPAIR wrapper data register as shown in Table 94 will be
                connected between WSI and WSO.
                               Pr




                Figure 90 illustrates the interaction between SOFT_LANE_REPAIR and HARD_LANE_ REPAIR
                instructions and the associated registers. It is pointed out that the actual I/O lane remapping is
                derived from the content of the lane repair shadow register.
                CaptureWR: when either SOFT_LANE_REPAIR or HARD_LANE_REPAIR is the current
                instruction, the CaptureWR event will load the lane remapping data from the lane repair shadow
                register into the shift stage of the WDR. This internal lane repair shadow register is pre-loaded with
                the repair data from a preceding HARD_LANE_REPAIR operation upon HBM3 DRAM initialization
                (RESET_n pulled LOW). The memory controller may use these data to configure the lane repair
                accordingly at the host; it may also use these data as a seed value for subsequent lane repair
                operations.
                UpdateWR (SOFT_LANE_REPAIR): when SOFT_LANE_REPAIR is the current instruction, the
                UpdateWR event will load the lane remapping data from the shift stage of the WDR into the lane
                repair shadow register and force the I/O lanes to be remapped accordingly. This remapping is non-
                persistent; it will be lost when RESET_n is pulled LOW or the device loses power. Pulling WRST_n
                LOW does not reset the lane repair shadow register.
                UpdateWR (HARD_LANE_REPAIR): when HARD_LANE_REPAIR is the current instruction, the
                UpdateWR event will load the lane remapping data from the shift stage of the WDR into the hard
                lane repair register. The controller must wait tHLREP to allow the device to complete this operation
                and permanently store the repair vector.

Micron mt65b24g - HBM3 24GB/36GB
Rev. L 06/2025                                                    161
                                                  Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                               24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM
                                                                                                       IEEE1500 Test Port

                Only a single broken lane can be repaired at a time, in order to limit the current constraint of the
                associated circuits. If multiple lanes are to be repaired, it is required to shift in the repair vectors for
                each broken lane sequentially, with all other lane repair setting = FH, and initiate each actual lane
                repair with a separate UpdateWR event.
                The UpdateWR event itself does not lead to an actual re-mapping of the I/O lanes. For such re-
                mapping to get effective it is required to initiate a chip reset by pulling RESET_n LOW for at least
                t
                 PW_RESET, which copies the repair vector from the hard lane repair register into the lane repair
                shadow register as shown in Figure 90.
                A stable WRCK clock is required during tSLREP and tHLREP times.
