CHANNEL_DISABLE
                This instruction disables one channel or all channels as specified in WIR[12:8]. The instruction may
                only be issued after tINIT3 timing has been met following a chip reset with RESET_n being pulled
                LOW and only before the CK clock is started for the first time. The disabled channel(s) will transi-
                tion into a safe low-power state where they do not respond to commands. All AWORD and
                DWORD input and output buffers including CK_t/CK_c and WDQS_t/ WDQS_c inputs of the
                disabled channel(s) will be turned off, thus allowing all external signals to float. The channel(s) will
                also not respond to EXTEXT_RX, EXTEST_TX and CHANNEL_ID instructions. Both RESET_n
                and WRST_n must be maintained HIGH during the all-channel disable state. The channel’s WSO
                output(s) will remain active and drive a LOW.
                The all-channel disable option shall be used during host-side HTOL and/or other reliability tests to
                prevent unintentional degradation of the HBM3 DRAM. This option may only be issued after tINIT3
                timing has been met, before the CK clock is started for the first time after exit from reset state, and
                only if no other IEEE1500 instruction except BYPASS or DEVICE_ID has been loaded before.
                A disabled channel can be enabled again by pulling both RESET_n and WRST_n to LOW and
                following the procedure described in the Initialization Sequence with Stable Power section.
                Wrapper Data Register: when CHANNEL_DISABLE is the current instruction, the data register as
                shown in Table 95 will be connected between WSI and WSO.

Rev. L 06/2025                                                     164
                                                    Micron Confidential and Proprietary

                                                                                                     24GB / 36GB HBM3 DRAM

                no effect.
                UpdateWR: when CHANNEL_DISABLE is the current instruction, the UpdateWR event will load
                the disable bit from the shift stage into the update stage of the WDR and asynchronously transition
                into a safe low power state when the bit is 1. Input and output buffers will be disabled latest after
                t
                 CHDIS.

WOSC_RUN and WOSC_COUNT
                The WOSC_RUN and WOSC_COUNT instructions are associated with the WDQS Interval
                Oscillator in the HBM3 DRAM.
                Wrapper Data Register: when WOSC_RUN is the current instruction, the WOSC_RUN data
                register as shown in Table 97 is connected between WSI and WSO[a:p], and the WSO outputs of
                all active channels drive the same data during ShiftWR events.
                When WOSC_COUNT is the current instruction, the WOSC_COUNT data register as shown in
                Table 98 is connected between WSI and WSO[a:p], and the WSO outputs of all active channels
                drive the same data during ShiftWR events.
                CaptureWR: when WOSC_RUN is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will have no
                effect. When WOSC_COUNT is the current instruction, the CaptureWR event will load the WDQS
                oscillator count value into the shift stage of the WDR and update the WOSC_COUNT_VALID field
                of the WDR.

HS_REP_CAP
                The HS_REP_CAP instruction tells the host whether a bank(s) has resources for either hard repair,
                soft repair or self repair. For each bank the gray-coded encoding indicates whether there are no
                resources, 1 resource, or 2 or more resources.
                This instruction shall be used by the host before performing any soft, hard or self repair. This
                register will be updated with the completion of a hard repair or a self repair.
                Wrapper Data Register: when HS_REP_CAP is the current instruction, the data register as shown
                in Table 102 is connected between WSI and WSO.

                                                                                                   Boundary Scan


Boundary Scan
                The HBM3 DRAM supports a boundary scan chain per channel via the IEEE1500 test port. The
                boundary scan operation is associated with IEEE1500 test port instructions EXTEST_RX and
                EXTEST_TX.
                Scan data is shifted in through WSI and out through the respective WSO, based on the active
                channel selections in the WIR (see Table 75). All functional signals are included in the boundary
                scan chains. Table 6 lists the micro-bump boundary scan chain order. Bit position 0 is the first bit
                shifted in on WSI and out on the WSOs.
                Three global signals in the MIDSTACK area are routed to the channel n and o scan chains:
                TEMP[1:0] are associated with channel n, and CATTRIP is associated with channel o. The
                boundary scan chain length for all channels is 122 bits (see Table 78), with dummy WDR bit




                                                                     A
                padding as needed on the MSB end of the chains. Matched length boundary scan chains allow all




                                                                    D
                channel chains to be loaded with matching data with one shift operation when WIR[12:8] = 1Fh.



                                                             rN
                All input-only and output-only signals are implemented as bi-directional I/Os to aid in SIP package
                level testing and fault isolation. Effectively, all signals support both EXTEST_RX and EXTEST_TX
                instructions.
                                                       de
                I/O signals power up in input mode by default. The host will put all AWORD and DWORD drivers
                                                 un

                into High-Z state prior to loading the EXTEST_TX instruction into the WIR. As soon as
                EXTEST_TX becomes the current instruction, all AWORD and DWORD signals will change to
                output mode and the outputs will drive the values shifted into the WDR shift stage.
                                         ed



                When EXTEST_RX is the current instruction, all functional signals of the selected channel(s) enter
                a High-Z state, including the output-only signals AERR, DERR, RDQS_t/RDQS_c, TEMP and
                                   id




                CATTRIP. On a subsequent CaptureWR event the signals will capture the input values into the
                WDR shift stage.
                                 ov




                Boundary scan mode entry may be asserted at any time after device initialization and before
                               Pr




                normal memory operation has commenced, e.g. before the CK clock has started to toggle. Upon
                exiting the boundary scan mode, the state of the HBM3 DRAM is unknown and the integrity of the
                data content of the memory array is not guaranteed and therefore the reset initialization sequence
                is required before returning to normal operation.

                The data input receiver mask for voltage and timing as shown in the figure below applies to each
                input receiver. The eye mask (VDIVW, tDIVW) defines the area the input signal must not encroach in
                order for the data input receiver to successfully capture an input signal with a BER of lower than
                TBD. The mask is a receiver property.
                Vcent_DQ(pin_mid) is defined as the midpoint between the largest Vcent_DQ voltage level and the smallest
                Vcent_DQ voltage level across all DQ pins for a given DRAM TBD (determined by DRAM VREFD
                training granularity, i.e. component/channel/DWORD) level. Each DQ Vcent is defined by the center,
                i.e. widest opening, of the cumulative data input eye as depicted in Figure 104.This clarifies that
                any DRAM TBD level variation must be accounted for within the DRAM data input receiver mask.

IDD Specification

IDD, IDDQL and IPP Specification Parameters and Test Conditions
                This chapter defines operating current measurement conditions.
                •    IDD currents are measured as time-averaged currents with all VDDC and VDDQ microbumps of the
                     HBM3 DRAM under test tied together.
                •    IDDQL currents use the same definitions as IDD except that the current on the VDDQL supply is
                     measured. All VDDQL microbumps of the HBM3 DRAM under test are tied together for IPP current
                     measurements. The output reference load CTOTAL is 2.5pF.
                •    IPP currents use the same definitions as IDD except that the current on the VPP supply is




                                                                       A
                     measured. All VPP microbumps of the HBM3 DRAM under test are tied together for IPP current




                                                                      D
                     measurements.



                                                             rN
                •    IDD, IDDQL and IPP measurements are taken with all channels of the HBM3 DRAM simultaneously
                     executing the same pattern.
                                                       de
                For IDD measurements, the following definitions apply:
                •    “0B“ and “LOW” are defined as VIN ≤ VIL(max);
                                                 un

                •    “1B“ and “HIGH” are defined as VIN ≥ VIH(min);
                •    WL, RL and RTP fields in MR1, MR2 and MR5, respectively, are programmed to appropriate
                                          ed



                     values;
                •
                                   id




                     Write DBI and read DBI are enabled in MR0 OP[1:0];
                •
                                 ov




                     Command/address parity and data parity are disabled in MR0 OP[6:4];
                •    Meta data is enabled in MR9 OP0;
                               Pr




                •    Error severity reporting are disabled in MR9 OP1;
                •    CNOP/RNOP commands and all address inputs are stable during idle command cycles;
                •    Basic IDD measurement conditions are described in Table 120. IDD measurements are done
                     after properly initializing the HBM3 DRAM. This includes the pre-load of the memory array with
                     data pattern used with IDD4R and IDD7 measurements.
                •    Timing parameters tRAS, tRP, tRREFD, tRFCab and tRFCpb are used as given in Table 121. If
                     not already an integer, round up to the next integer.
                •    Data pattern used with IDD4R, IDD4W and IDD7 measurements (BL8, per data byte):
                     Pattern A: 00h, 3Ch, F0h, 69h, AAh, FFh, C3h, 55h
                     Pattern B: F0h, A5h, 96h, 0Fh, C3h, 55h, CCh, 5Ah

AC Timings

Data Input Timings Considerations
                All WDQS-to-DQ timings are measured from WDQS to the center (midpoint) of the tDIVW window
                taken at the VDIVW voltage levels centered around Vcent_DQ(pin_mid). The timings at the inputs are
                referenced with respect to all data signal groups center aligned to the DRAM internal latch. The
                data-to-data offset within a write de-skew group, tDQ2DQtra _I, is defined as the difference
                between the minimum and maximum tWDQS2DQ_I for a given de-skew group. The data-to-data
                offset between different de-skew groups, tDQ2DQter _I, is defined as the difference between the
                minimum and maximum tWDQS2DQ_I for a whole DWORD.

Data Output Timings Considerations
                The data-to-data offset within a read de-skew group, tDQ2DQtra _O, is defined as the difference
                between the earliest and the latest valid transition for a given de-skew group. The data-to-data
                offset between different de-skew groups, tDQ2DQter _O, is defined as the difference between the
                earliest and the latest valid transition for a whole DWORD. tWDQS2DQ_O is defined as the WDQS
                to read data and RDQS offset.

                                                                                                          Microbump Matrix


Microbump Matrix
                The microbump matrix of the HBM3 DRAM employs a staggered pattern as depicted in Figure 113
                where a ‘staggered’ bump is located halfway between major row and column, hence its location is
                determined by X/2 and Y/2. Table 130 shows geometric parameters of the staggered micro bump
                pattern. Parameter PMIN is the minimum bump pitch anywhere in the microbump field.

                Figure 113: Staggered Microbump Pattern

                                                     X
                                                         X/2




                                                                                    A
                                                                                   D
                                                                         Y/2
                                                                     rN        Y
                                                               de
                                                                                      SoC
                                                         un
                                                 ed
                                   id
                                 ov
                               Pr




                 Table 130: Geometric Parameters of the Staggered Microbump Pattern
                   Label           Nominal Value                     Description
                       X               96µm         Horizontal pitch of two adjacent micro bumps
                       Y              110µm         Vertical pitch of two adjacent micro bumps
                     PMIN              73µm         Minimum pitch of the bump field
                       D               28µm         Microbump diameter
                       S              PMIN - D      Bump-to-bump air gap


                The bump matrix consists of a total of 7775 bumps arranged in 148 columns with a pitch of X/2 and
                161 rows with a pitch of Y/2. The overall array size is (147 × X/2 + D)µm × (160 × Y/2 + D)µm =
                7084μm × 8828μm.
                The ball matrix is center aligned with the die. The ball array center is the origin of the ball location
                coordinates. Ball A1 is located at the top left at X = -3528μm, Y = +4400μm.
                A geographical overview of the microbump matrix is provided in Figure 114, and the detailed bump
                matrices are provided in Table 132 (Part 1) thru Table 136 (Part 5). Due to space constraints these
                tables use abbreviations for specific functions as given in Table 131.
